requirements.text: An approval mark described in paragraph 5.3. shall be affixed to every ESA conforming to a type approved under this Regulation, except that no marking is required for electrical/electronic systems built into vehicles which are approved as units.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the lamp/ESA for presence of the R10 approval mark.
requirements.why: The lamp's LED/PCB electronics are approved as an ESA under R10 and must carry the mark.

requirements.text: The international approval mark shall be affixed in a conspicuous and easily accessible place specified on the approval communication form.
requirements.test_case: Compare the mark location on the sample with the location specified on the communication form.
requirements.why: Defines where the ESA approval mark must be placed.

requirements.text: The approval mark shall comprise a circle containing the letter "E", followed by the distinguishing number of the country granting the approval.
requirements.test_case: Visually inspect the mark for the circled E and the country number.
requirements.why: Mandatory content of the ESA approval mark.

requirements.text: The approval mark shall comprise the number of this Regulation, followed by the letter "R", a dash and the approval number to the right of the circle specified in paragraph 5.3.1.
requirements.test_case: Visually inspect the mark for '10R-' followed by the approval number to the right of the circle.
requirements.why: Mandatory content of the ESA approval mark.

requirements.text: The approval mark shall be laid out according to Model A or Model B, with dimension a = 6 mm min.
requirements.test_case: Measure the height dimension 'a' of the marking and verify it is at least 6 mm.
requirements.why: Annex 1 sets the minimum size of the mark the ESA carries.

requirements.text: Markings on ESAs in conformity with paragraph 5.3. need not be visible when the ESA is installed in the vehicle.
requirements.test_case: Confirm the mark is present on the ESA, even if it is hidden after installation.
requirements.why: Clarifies the visibility condition for the mark on the lamp ESA.

requirements.text: The ESA(s) (LED modules on PCB of the rear lamp) shall be designed, constructed and fitted in such a way as to enable the vehicle, in normal conditions of use, to comply with the requirements of this Regulation.
requirements.test_case: Review the design and EMC test results of the LED module ESA against all UN R10 limits under normal operating conditions.
requirements.why: The lamp contains an electronic sub-assembly (LED modules with circuitry) that falls under R10 as an ESA.

requirements.text: The ESA shall be tested for radiated and conducted emissions, and for immunity to radiated and conducted disturbances.
requirements.test_case: Perform radiated and conducted emission tests and radiated and conducted immunity tests on the LED module ESA per the R10 annexes.
requirements.why: ESA approval of the lamp electronics requires all four emission and immunity test categories.

requirements.text: The ESA shall be tested according to a test plan containing at least the mode of operation, stimulated function(s), monitored function(s), pass/fail criterion(criteria) and intended emissions.
requirements.test_case: Check that the EMC test plan defines operating modes (position, stop, reversing lamp ON) and the monitored functions and pass/fail criteria, and that the tests are performed in these modes.
requirements.why: The test plan defines the operating modes and pass/fail criteria the lamp ESA must meet during EMC testing.

requirements.text: The electromagnetic radiation generated by the ESA (LED modules on PCB) representative of its type shall be measured by the method described in Annex 7.
requirements.test_case: Confirm the broadband emission test report for the LED module ESA uses the Annex 7 (CISPR 25 ALSE) method.
requirements.why: The lamp's LED modules with circuitry are an ESA whose broadband emissions are regulated by R10.

requirements.text: When measurements are made using the method described in Annex 7, the ESA broadband limit shall be 62 to 52 dB microvolts/m in the 30 to 75 MHz frequency band, this limit decreasing logarithmically with frequencies above 30 MHz.
requirements.test_case: Measure radiated broadband emissions 30-75 MHz in an ALSE and compare against the log-decreasing 62-52 dBµV/m limit line.
requirements.why: Sets the broadband emission limit for the ESA in the 30-75 MHz band.

requirements.text: When measurements are made using the method described in Annex 7, the ESA broadband limit shall be 52 to 63 dB microvolts/m in the 75 to 400 MHz frequency band, this limit increasing logarithmically with frequencies above 75 MHz as shown in Appendix 6.
requirements.test_case: Measure radiated broadband emissions 75-400 MHz and compare against the log-increasing 52-63 dBµV/m limit line.
requirements.why: Sets the broadband emission limit for the ESA in the 75-400 MHz band.

requirements.text: When measurements are made using the method described in Annex 7, the ESA broadband limit shall remain constant at 63 dB microvolts/m in the 400 to 1,000 MHz frequency band.
requirements.test_case: Measure radiated broadband emissions 400-1,000 MHz and verify all readings are below 63 dBµV/m.
requirements.why: Sets the broadband emission limit for the ESA in the 400-1,000 MHz band.

requirements.text: On the ESA representative of its type, the measured broadband emission values, expressed in dB microvolts/m, shall be below the type approval limits.
requirements.test_case: Review the emission spectrum over 30-1,000 MHz and confirm every characteristic reading lies below the limit line.
requirements.why: Pass/fail criterion for the LED module ESA broadband emissions.

requirements.text: During the broadband emission test the ESA under test shall be in normal operation mode, preferably in maximum load.
requirements.test_case: Verify test plan operates the LED modules with all lamp functions (position, stop, reversing) energised at maximum load during measurement.
requirements.why: Defines the operating state of the lamp ESA under which the emission limits must be met.

requirements.text: For an ESA other than involved in REESS charging mode coupled to the power grid, the broadband emission test shall be performed according to the ALSE method described in Clause 6.4 of CISPR 25.
requirements.test_case: Check test report states the CISPR 25 Clause 6.4 ALSE set-up was used.
requirements.why: The lamp ESA is not a charging ESA, so the ALSE method applies to it.

requirements.text: The broadband emission limits shall apply throughout the frequency range 30 to 1,000 MHz for measurements performed in an ALSE or OATS.
requirements.test_case: Confirm the measurement covers the complete 30-1,000 MHz range.
requirements.why: Defines the frequency range over which the ESA must comply.

requirements.text: The broadband limits are for quasi-peak detectors; if peak detectors are used a correction factor of 20 dB as defined in CISPR 12 shall be applied.
requirements.test_case: Check the detector type used and, for peak measurements, that the 20 dB correction was applied before comparison with the limit.
requirements.why: Determines how the ESA's measured values are compared with the limits.

requirements.text: The electromagnetic radiation (narrowband) generated by the ESA representative of its type shall be measured by the method described in Annex 8.
requirements.test_case: Perform CISPR 25 ALSE narrowband emission test per Annex 8 with average detector on the LED module ESA in normal operation mode.
requirements.why: The LED modules on PCB are an ESA, which is subject to the R10 narrowband emission measurement.

requirements.text: When measurements are made using the method described in Annex 8, the ESA narrowband limits shall be 52 to 42 dB microvolts/m in the 30 to 75 MHz frequency band, this limit decreasing logarithmically with frequencies above 30 MHz.
requirements.test_case: Compare average-detector radiated emission readings from 30 to 75 MHz against the logarithmically decreasing 52–42 dBµV/m limit line.
requirements.why: The LED/PCB ESA must not exceed the narrowband radiated emission limits in this band.

requirements.text: When measurements are made using the method described in Annex 8, the ESA narrowband limits shall be 42 to 53 dB microvolts/m in the 75 to 400 MHz band, this limit increasing logarithmically with frequencies above 75 MHz as shown in Appendix 7.
requirements.test_case: Compare average-detector radiated emission readings from 75 to 400 MHz against the logarithmically increasing 42–53 dBµV/m limit line.
requirements.why: The LED/PCB ESA must not exceed the narrowband radiated emission limits in this band.

requirements.text: When measurements are made using the method described in Annex 8, the ESA narrowband limit in the 400 to 1,000 MHz frequency band shall remain constant at 53 dB microvolts/m.
requirements.test_case: Compare average-detector radiated emission readings from 400 to 1,000 MHz against the 53 dBµV/m limit.
requirements.why: The LED/PCB ESA must not exceed the narrowband radiated emission limit in this band.

requirements.text: On the ESA representative of its type, the measured narrowband value, expressed in dB microvolts/m, shall be below the type approval limits.
requirements.test_case: Verify that all characteristic readings (max of horizontal/vertical polarisation) in the test report are below the limit line at every frequency from 30 to 1,000 MHz.
requirements.why: This is the pass/fail criterion for narrowband emissions of the lamp's ESA.

requirements.text: The immunity to electromagnetic radiation of the ESA representative of its type shall be tested by the method(s) chosen from those described in Annex 9 (absorber chamber ISO 11452-2, TEM cell ISO 11452-3, BCI ISO 11452-4, stripline ISO 11452-5, reverberation chamber ISO 11452-11), covering the full 20 to 6,000 MHz frequency range.
requirements.test_case: Review the EMC test plan/report to confirm the chosen Annex 9 methods together cover 20 to 6,000 MHz.
requirements.why: The LED module PCB is an ESA subject to R10 radiated immunity approval.

requirements.text: When tested with the stripline method, the ESA shall withstand a test level of 60 V/m in the 20 to 400 MHz range over more than 90 per cent of the 20 to 6,000 MHz frequency band (Table 2a).
requirements.test_case: Stripline test per ISO 11452-5 at 60 V/m, 20-400 MHz, with the lamp functions monitored.
requirements.why: Applies to the lamp ESA if the stripline method is chosen.

requirements.text: When tested with the TEM cell method, the ESA shall withstand a test level of 75 V/m in the 20 to 200 MHz range over more than 90 per cent of the 20 to 6,000 MHz frequency band (Table 2a).
requirements.test_case: TEM cell test per ISO 11452-3 at 75 V/m, 20-200 MHz.
requirements.why: Applies to the lamp ESA if the TEM cell method is chosen.

requirements.text: When tested with the BCI method, the ESA shall withstand a test level of 60 mA in the 20 to 400 MHz range over more than 90 per cent of the 20 to 6,000 MHz frequency band (Table 2a).
requirements.test_case: BCI test per ISO 11452-4 at 60 mA, 20-400 MHz.
requirements.why: Applies to the lamp ESA if the BCI method is chosen.

requirements.text: When tested with the ALSE (absorber chamber) method, the ESA shall withstand 30 V/m in the 80 to 2,000 MHz range and 10 V/m in the 2,000 to 6,000 MHz range over more than 90 per cent of the 20 to 6,000 MHz frequency band (Table 2a).
requirements.test_case: ALSE test per ISO 11452-2, vertical polarisation, at 30 V/m (80-2,000 MHz) and 10 V/m (2-6 GHz).
requirements.why: Applies to the lamp ESA if the absorber chamber method is chosen.

requirements.text: When tested with the reverberation chamber method, the ESA shall withstand 21 V/m from LUF to 2,000 MHz and 7 V/m in the 2,000 to 6,000 MHz range over more than 90 per cent of the 20 to 6,000 MHz frequency band (Table 2a).
requirements.test_case: Reverberation chamber test per ISO 11452-11 at 21 V/m (LUF-2,000 MHz) and 7 V/m (2-6 GHz).
requirements.why: Applies to the lamp ESA if the reverberation chamber method is chosen.

requirements.text: When tested with the stripline method, the ESA shall withstand a minimum test level of 50 V/m in the 20 to 400 MHz range over the whole 20 to 6,000 MHz frequency band (Table 2b).
requirements.test_case: Confirm no frequency point in the stripline test was below 50 V/m.
requirements.why: Minimum immunity level for the lamp ESA over the whole band.

requirements.text: When tested with the TEM cell method, the ESA shall withstand a minimum test level of 62,5 V/m in the 20 to 200 MHz range over the whole 20 to 6,000 MHz frequency band (Table 2b).
requirements.test_case: Confirm no frequency point in the TEM cell test was below 62,5 V/m.
requirements.why: Minimum immunity level for the lamp ESA over the whole band.

requirements.text: When tested with the BCI method, the ESA shall withstand a minimum test level of 50 mA in the 20 to 400 MHz range over the whole 20 to 6,000 MHz frequency band (Table 2b).
requirements.test_case: Confirm no frequency point in the BCI test was below 50 mA.
requirements.why: Minimum immunity level for the lamp ESA over the whole band.

requirements.text: When tested with the ALSE method, the ESA shall withstand a minimum test level of 25 V/m in the 80 to 2,000 MHz range and 8 V/m in the 2,000 to 6,000 MHz range over the whole 20 to 6,000 MHz frequency band (Table 2b).
requirements.test_case: Confirm no frequency point in the ALSE test was below 25 V/m (80-2,000 MHz) or 8 V/m (2-6 GHz).
requirements.why: Minimum immunity level for the lamp ESA over the whole band.

requirements.text: When tested with the reverberation chamber method, the ESA shall withstand a minimum test level of 18 V/m from LUF to 2,000 MHz and 6 V/m in the 2,000 to 6,000 MHz range over the whole 20 to 6,000 MHz frequency band (Table 2b).
requirements.test_case: Confirm no frequency point in the reverberation chamber test was below 18 V/m (LUF-2,000 MHz) or 6 V/m (2-6 GHz).
requirements.why: Minimum immunity level for the lamp ESA over the whole band.

requirements.text: During the tests performed in accordance with Annex 9, there shall be no degradation of performance of the "immunity related functions" of the ESA.
requirements.test_case: Monitor the rear position, stop and reversing lamp outputs during exposure and verify no flicker, dropout or unintended activation.
requirements.why: Pass/fail criterion for radiated immunity of the lamp ESA, whose lighting functions are immunity related.

requirements.text: During the immunity tests the ESA under test shall be switched on and stimulated to be in normal operation condition.
requirements.test_case: Verify the test report shows each lamp function energised in normal operating mode during exposure.
requirements.why: Test condition constraining the operating state of the lamp ESA during immunity testing.

requirements.text: The immunity measurements shall be made in the 20 to 6,000 MHz frequency range using AM (1 kHz, 80 per cent modulation depth) in 20 to 400 MHz, PM2 (Ton 3 µs, period 3,333 µs) in 2,700 to 3,100 MHz, and PM3 (Ton 500 µs, period 1,000 µs) in 380 to 2,700 MHz and 3,100 to 6,000 MHz.
requirements.test_case: Check the test report confirms the modulation types and frequency ranges applied.
requirements.why: Test condition defining the disturbance the lamp ESA must withstand.

requirements.text: Where the ESA (LED modules on PCB with driver circuitry) does not include an electronic oscillator with an operating frequency greater than 9 kHz, it shall be deemed to comply with paragraph 6.6.2. (ESA radiated narrowband emission limits) and with Annex 8.
requirements.test_case: Review the LED driver schematic and BOM for any oscillator, switching regulator or microcontroller clock above 9 kHz; if none, document the exemption, otherwise perform the Annex 8 narrowband emission test.
requirements.why: The lamp's LED PCB is an ESA, and its narrowband emission compliance route depends on whether the driver contains an oscillator above 9 kHz.

requirements.text: ESAs with no immunity related functions need not be tested for immunity to radiated disturbances and shall be deemed to comply with paragraph 6.8. and with Annex 9; where the ESA performs immunity related functions (e.g. stop lamp and rear position lamp lighting), it shall be tested for radiated immunity.
requirements.test_case: Assess the ESA functions against the immunity related functions definition; stop and position lighting are immunity related, so perform the Annex 9 radiated immunity test and check that the lamps do not switch off or activate unexpectedly.
requirements.why: Whether the LED ESA is exempt from the Annex 9 radiated immunity test depends on its immunity related functions (stop lights, rear lights).

requirements.text: ESAs that are not switched, contain no switches or do not include inductive load need not be tested for transient conducted emission on 12/24 V supply lines and shall be deemed to comply with paragraph 6.7.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the LED driver circuit for switches, switched operation and inductive loads (e.g. buck/boost inductors); if any are present, perform the ISO 7637-2 transient conducted emission test per paragraph 6.7.
requirements.why: The lamp ESA is supplied from the 12/24 V vehicle supply, and its transient conducted emission test exemption depends on its switching and inductive-load content.

requirements.text: The conformity of production of the ESA shall comply with the procedures set out in Schedule 1 of the 1958 Agreement (E/ECE/TRANS/505/Rev.3), together with the requirements of paragraph 9.
requirements.test_case: Audit the CoP plan and records of the LED module ESA against Schedule 1 of the 1958 Agreement.
requirements.why: The LED PCB modules are an ESA approved under R10, so their series production falls under R10 CoP.

requirements.text: ESAs approved under this Regulation shall be so manufactured as to conform to the approved type by meeting the requirements set forth in paragraph 6. and, if applicable, in paragraph 7.
requirements.test_case: Take series samples of the LED module ESA and repeat the paragraph 6 EMC tests to confirm conformity with the approved type.
requirements.why: The series-produced rear-lamp ESA must keep the EMC performance of the approved type.

requirements.text: Conformity of production of the ESA shall be checked on the basis of the data contained in the communication form(s) for type approval set out in Annex 3A and/or 3B.
requirements.test_case: Compare series ESA configuration and test data with the Annex 3B communication form data.
requirements.why: Series ESAs must match the data declared in the approval communication form.

requirements.text: When the conformity of an ESA taken from the series is verified, the measured broadband electromagnetic radiated emission levels shall not exceed by more than 4 dB (60 per cent) the reference limits of paragraph 6.5.2.1. (62 to 52 dB microvolts/m in 30 to 75 MHz decreasing logarithmically, 52 to 63 dB microvolts/m in 75 to 400 MHz increasing logarithmically, 63 dB microvolts/m constant in 400 to 1,000 MHz, measured per Annex 7).
requirements.test_case: Measure broadband radiated emissions of a series ESA per Annex 7 and check that levels are at most 4 dB above the 6.5.2.1 limits.
requirements.why: The LED module ESA with driver circuitry can generate broadband emissions and is subject to CoP emission limits.

requirements.text: When the conformity of an ESA taken from the series is verified, the measured narrowband electromagnetic radiated emission levels shall not exceed by more than 4 dB (60 per cent) the reference limits of paragraph 6.6.2.1. (52 to 42 dB microvolts/m in 30 to 75 MHz decreasing logarithmically, 42 to 53 dB microvolts/m in 75 to 400 MHz increasing logarithmically, 53 dB microvolts/m constant in 400 to 1,000 MHz, measured per Annex 8).
requirements.test_case: Measure narrowband radiated emissions of a series ESA per Annex 8 and check that levels are at most 4 dB above the 6.6.2.1 limits.
requirements.why: The ESA may contain oscillators or microcontrollers producing narrowband emissions subject to CoP limits.

requirements.text: When the conformity of an ESA taken from the series is verified, the ESA shall not exhibit any degradation relating to the direct control of the vehicle which could be observed by the driver or other road users when subjected to a field strength up to 80 per cent of the reference limits prescribed in paragraph 6.8.2.1. (Tables 2a/2b, e.g. ALSE 30 V/m for 80 to 2,000 MHz and 10 V/m for 2,000 to 6,000 MHz; BCI 60 mA for 20 to 400 MHz).
requirements.test_case: Expose a series ESA per Annex 9 at 80 per cent of the Table 2a/2b levels and monitor for unintended switching or dropout of the stop, position and reversing light outputs.
requirements.why: Rear lighting and stop-light functions are immunity-related, so series ESAs must keep radiated immunity at CoP level.

requirements.text: When the conformity of a component or STU taken from the series is verified, the ESA shall show no degradation of performance of immunity related functions up to the conducted transient levels given in paragraph 6.9.1. (ISO 16750-2 starting profile and ISO 7637-2 pulses 1, 2a, 2b, 3a and 3b per Tables 3a and 3b, e.g. 12 V system: -75 V, +37 V, +10 V, -112 V, +75 V).
requirements.test_case: Apply ISO 7637-2 pulses and the ISO 16750-2 starting profile to a series ESA per Annex 10 and verify that the FPSC/functional status meets Tables 3a/3b.
requirements.why: The lamp ESA is connected to the vehicle supply and its lighting functions must withstand conducted transients in series production.

requirements.text: When the conformity of a component or STU taken from the series is verified, the conducted transient emission of the ESA shall not exceed the levels given in paragraph 6.7.1. (Table 1: +75 V / -100 V for vehicles with 12 V systems; +150 V / -450 V for vehicles with 24 V systems).
requirements.test_case: Measure conducted emission pulses on the supply lines of a series ESA per ISO 7637-2 (Annex 10) and check them against the Table 1 maximum amplitudes.
requirements.why: The switched LED driver ESA can emit conducted transients onto the vehicle supply and must meet the CoP limits.

requirements.text: The broadband electromagnetic emission test of the ESA shall be performed according to CISPR 25, if not otherwise stated in Annex 7.
requirements.test_case: Review the EMC test plan and report to confirm that broadband emission testing follows CISPR 25.
requirements.why: The LED/PCB modules are an ESA whose broadband emissions are tested by Annex 7.

requirements.text: The ESA under test shall be in normal operation mode, preferably in maximum load, during the broadband emission test.
requirements.test_case: Energise all lamp functions (position, stop, reversing) at nominal voltage during the measurement and record the operating state.
requirements.why: This defines the operating state of the lamp's LED ESA during the emission test.

requirements.text: For ESA other than involved in "REESS charging mode coupled to the power grid", the broadband emission test shall be performed according to the ALSE method described in Clause 6.4 of CISPR 25.
requirements.test_case: Verify that the test set-up in the ALSE follows CISPR 25 Clause 6.4 (ground plane, harness and antenna positions).
requirements.why: The lamp ESA is not a REESS charging ESA, so the ALSE method applies to it.

requirements.text: The ambient extraneous noise or signal, measured before or after the main test, shall be at least 6 dB below the limits of interference given in paragraph 6.5.2.1., except for intentional narrowband ambient transmissions.
requirements.test_case: Perform an ambient scan with the ESA off and confirm the noise floor is at least 6 dB below the 6.5.2.1 limit line.
requirements.why: This is a validity condition on the measurement used to judge the ESA's emissions.

requirements.text: The broadband emission limits shall apply throughout the frequency range 30 to 1,000 MHz for measurements performed in an ALSE or OATS.
requirements.test_case: Scan the ESA's radiated emissions from 30 to 1,000 MHz and compare them with the limit.
requirements.why: This sets the frequency range over which the ESA must meet the broadband limits.

requirements.text: If peak detectors are used for the broadband emission measurement, a correction factor of 20 dB as defined in CISPR 12 shall be applied to the quasi-peak limits given in paragraphs 6.5. and 7.10.
requirements.test_case: Check that peak-detector results are evaluated against the quasi-peak limit with the 20 dB CISPR 12 correction applied.
requirements.why: This determines the pass/fail evaluation of the ESA's emissions.

requirements.text: The broadband emission measurements shall be performed with a spectrum analyser or a scanning receiver using the parameters defined in Table 1 and Table 2.
requirements.test_case: Verify the instrument type and settings recorded in the test report.
requirements.why: This is the measurement method constraint for the ESA's compliance.

requirements.text: When a spectrum analyser is used in the 30 to 1,000 MHz range, the following settings shall apply: for the peak detector, an RBW at -3 dB of 100/120 kHz and a minimum scan time of 100 ms/MHz; for the quasi-peak detector, an RBW at -6 dB of 120 kHz and a minimum scan time of 20 s/MHz.
requirements.test_case: Check the spectrum analyser RBW and scan time settings against Table 1.
requirements.why: These Table 1 parameters govern the ESA emission measurement.

requirements.text: If a spectrum analyser is used for peak measurements, the video bandwidth shall be at least three times the resolution bandwidth (RBW).
requirements.test_case: Verify that the VBW setting is at least 3 x RBW.
requirements.why: This is a measurement condition for the ESA emission test.

requirements.text: When a scanning receiver is used in the 30 to 1,000 MHz range, the following settings shall apply: for the peak detector, a BW at -6 dB of 120 kHz, a maximum step size of 60 kHz and a minimum dwell time of 5 ms; for the quasi-peak detector, a BW at -6 dB of 120 kHz, a maximum step size of 60 kHz and a minimum dwell time of 1 s.
requirements.test_case: Check the receiver bandwidth, step size and dwell time settings against Table 2.
requirements.why: These Table 2 parameters govern the ESA emission measurement.

requirements.text: FFT-based measuring instruments shall continuously record and evaluate the signal during the measurement time, with a minimum measurement time of 1 s per analysis frequency band (in real-time mode).
requirements.test_case: If an FFT receiver is used, confirm real-time mode and a dwell time of at least 1 s per analysis band.
requirements.why: This is a measurement condition for the ESA emission test.

requirements.text: Unless otherwise specified, the configuration with the LV harness closer to the antenna shall be tested.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the set-up photos to confirm that the LV harness is on the antenna side.
requirements.why: This constrains the test configuration of the lamp ESA.

requirements.text: The phase centre of the antenna shall be in line with the centre of the longitudinal part of the wiring harnesses for frequencies up to 1,000 MHz.
requirements.test_case: Measure the antenna position relative to the centre of the harness.
requirements.why: This constrains the test configuration of the lamp ESA.

requirements.text: The ESA shall meet the requirements of Annex 7 when tested at the intervals specified in CISPR 12 throughout the frequency range 30 to 1,000 MHz, or alternatively at the 14 frequencies giving the highest emission levels within each of the 14 bands (30-34, 34-45, 45-60, 60-80, 80-100, 100-130, 130-170, 170-225, 225-300, 300-400, 400-525, 525-700, 700-850 and 850-1,000 MHz).
requirements.test_case: Run the full-band scan, or the 14-band spot check, and confirm that every reading is below the limit.
requirements.why: This is the pass criterion for the ESA's broadband emissions.

requirements.text: In the event that the limit is exceeded during the test, investigations shall be made to ensure that this is due to the ESA and not to background radiation.
requirements.test_case: For any exceedance, repeat the measurement with the ESA off to discriminate ESA emissions from ambient.
requirements.why: This determines the attribution of limit exceedances to the ESA.

requirements.text: The maximum of the readings relative to the limit (horizontal/vertical polarization) in each of the 14 frequency bands shall be taken as the characteristic reading at the frequency at which the measurements were made.
requirements.test_case: Measure in both antenna polarizations and report the worst-case margin per band.
requirements.why: This defines the evaluated value for the ESA's compliance.

requirements.text: Unless otherwise stated in Annex 8, the narrowband electromagnetic emission test of the ESA shall be performed according to CISPR 25.
requirements.test_case: Review the EMC test plan and report to confirm the narrowband emission test follows CISPR 25.
requirements.why: The lamp's LED modules on PCB are an ESA subject to the R10 narrowband emission test of Annex 8.

requirements.text: The ESA under test shall be in normal operation mode, preferably in maximum load, during the narrowband emission test.
requirements.test_case: Check the test report that rear position, stop and reversing LED functions were energised in normal operation at maximum load.
requirements.why: This defines the operating state in which the lamp ESA must meet the narrowband emission limits.

requirements.text: The narrowband emission test of the ESA shall be performed according to the ALSE method described in paragraph 6.4. of CISPR 25.
requirements.test_case: Verify the test set-up used the ALSE method of CISPR 25 clause 6.4, or an OATS complying with CISPR 16-1-4 as permitted by 3.2.
requirements.why: This is the mandatory test arrangement for the lamp ESA's narrowband emission compliance.

requirements.text: Ambient measurements shall be taken before or after the main test, and the extraneous noise or signal shall be at least 6 dB below the limits of interference given in paragraph 6.6.2.1., except for intentional narrowband ambient transmissions.
requirements.test_case: Perform an ambient scan with the ESA switched off and confirm the noise floor is at least 6 dB below the 6.6.2.1 limits.
requirements.why: This is a validity condition for the narrowband emission result of the lamp ESA.

requirements.text: The narrowband emission limits shall apply throughout the frequency range 30 to 1,000 MHz for measurements performed in an ALSE or OATS.
requirements.test_case: Scan the ESA emissions from 30 MHz to 1,000 MHz and compare them with the 6.6.2.1 limit line.
requirements.why: This sets the frequency range over which the lamp ESA must comply with the emission limits.

requirements.text: Narrowband emission measurements of the ESA shall be performed with an average detector.
requirements.test_case: Confirm the receiver detector setting is average in the test report.
requirements.why: The narrowband limits for the lamp ESA are evaluated with the average detector.

requirements.text: The narrowband emission measurements shall be performed with a spectrum analyser or a scanning receiver using the parameters defined in Tables 1 and 2.
requirements.test_case: Check the instrument type and its settings against Tables 1 and 2.
requirements.why: This constrains how compliance of the lamp ESA is measured.

requirements.text: When a spectrum analyser with the average detector is used over 30 to 1,000 MHz, the RBW at -3 dB shall be 100/120 kHz and the minimum scan time shall be 100 ms/MHz (Table 1).
requirements.test_case: Verify the spectrum analyser RBW and scan time settings in the test log.
requirements.why: These measurement parameters apply to the lamp ESA emission test.

requirements.text: When a scanning receiver with the average detector is used over 30 to 1,000 MHz, the BW at -6 dB shall be 120 kHz, the maximum step size shall be 60 kHz and the minimum dwell time shall be 5 ms (Table 2).
requirements.test_case: Verify the receiver bandwidth, step size and dwell time settings in the test log.
requirements.why: These measurement parameters apply to the lamp ESA emission test.

requirements.text: If a spectrum analyser is used for peak measurements, the video bandwidth shall be at least three times the resolution bandwidth (RBW).
requirements.test_case: Check that VBW is at least 3 x RBW in the analyser settings.
requirements.why: This is a measurement constraint for the lamp ESA emission test.

requirements.text: FFT-based measuring instruments shall continuously record and evaluate the signal during the measurement time.
requirements.test_case: Confirm the FFT receiver was operated in continuous real-time evaluation mode.
requirements.why: This is a measurement constraint for the lamp ESA emission test.

requirements.text: If FFT-based instruments are used, the minimum measurement time shall be 1 s per analysis frequency band (in real-time mode) of the FFT instrument.
requirements.test_case: Verify a measurement time of at least 1 s per FFT analysis band in the test log.
requirements.why: This is a measurement constraint for the lamp ESA emission test.

requirements.text: The test shall be performed at the intervals specified in the CISPR 12 standard throughout the frequency range 30 to 1,000 MHz, or alternatively at the 14 frequencies giving the highest emission levels within each of the 14 frequency bands, to confirm that the ESA meets the requirements of Annex 8.
requirements.test_case: Review the frequency points measured against CISPR 12 intervals or against the 14-band method.
requirements.why: The lamp ESA must meet the Annex 8 requirements at the frequencies tested.

requirements.text: In the event that the limit is exceeded during the test, investigations shall be made to ensure that this is due to the ESA and not to background radiation, including broadband radiation from the ESA.
requirements.test_case: For any exceedance, compare the result with an ambient scan and a broadband check to attribute it to the ESA's narrowband emission.
requirements.why: This determines whether the lamp ESA fails the narrowband emission limit.

requirements.text: The maximum of the readings relative to the limit (horizontal/vertical polarisation) in each of the 14 frequency bands shall be taken as the characteristic reading at the frequency at which the measurements were made.
requirements.test_case: Take the worst-case horizontal/vertical polarisation reading per band and compare it with the limit.
requirements.why: This defines the reading against which the lamp ESA compliance is judged.

requirements.text: The ESA shall comply with the requirements of any combination of the test methods (absorber chamber ISO 11452-2, TEM cell ISO 11452-3, BCI ISO 11452-4, stripline ISO 11452-5, reverberation chamber ISO 11452-11) provided that the results cover the full frequency range specified in paragraph 3.1. of Annex 9.
requirements.test_case: Review the immunity test plan and reports to confirm the selected methods together cover 20 to 6,000 MHz.
requirements.why: The LED module PCB is an ESA whose radiated immunity is verified by these methods.

requirements.text: The frequency range and general test conditions for ESA immunity testing shall be based on ISO 11452-1.
requirements.test_case: Check that the test report references ISO 11452-1 for frequency range and general conditions.
requirements.why: This sets the general test conditions applied to the lamp ESA.

requirements.text: The test conditions for the ESA shall be according to ISO 11452-1.
requirements.test_case: Audit the test setup against ISO 11452-1 conditions.
requirements.why: This constrains how the lamp ESA is tested for immunity.

requirements.text: The ESA under test shall be switched on and shall be stimulated to be in normal operation condition during the immunity tests.
requirements.test_case: Verify that the rear position, stop and reversing functions are energised and monitored during exposure.
requirements.why: The lamp functions must be operating when immunity is assessed.

requirements.text: The ESA under test shall be arranged as defined in Annex 9 unless individual test methods dictate otherwise.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the ESA arrangement against the Annex 9 and ISO setup drawings.
requirements.why: This defines the configuration of the product during the test.

requirements.text: If the ESA under test consists of more than one unit, the length of the interconnecting cables between the electronic control unit and the AN shall be as defined in the standard where the vehicle wiring harnesses are not available.
requirements.test_case: Measure the harness length between the ESA and the AN against the ISO 11452 value.
requirements.why: This constrains the harness configuration of a multi-unit lamp ESA during the test.

requirements.text: Immunity measurements on the ESA shall be made in the 20 to 6,000 MHz frequency range, with frequency steps according to ISO 11452-1.
requirements.test_case: Confirm the sweep covers 20 to 6,000 MHz with ISO 11452-1 step sizes.
requirements.why: This defines the frequency range over which the lamp ESA must remain immune.

requirements.text: The test signal modulation shall be AM (amplitude modulation), with 1 kHz modulation and 80 per cent modulation depth, in the 20 to 400 MHz frequency range.
requirements.test_case: Verify the signal generator settings for 20 to 400 MHz.
requirements.why: This sets the disturbance the ESA must withstand in this band.

requirements.text: The test signal modulation shall be PM2 (pulse modulation type 2), Ton 3 µs, period 3,333 µs, in the 2,700 to 3,100 MHz frequency range.
requirements.test_case: Verify the pulse modulation settings for 2,700 to 3,100 MHz.
requirements.why: This sets the disturbance the ESA must withstand in this band.

requirements.text: The test signal modulation shall be PM3 (pulse modulation type 3), Ton 500 µs, period 1,000 µs, in the 380 to 2,700 MHz and the 3,100 to 6,000 MHz frequency ranges.
requirements.test_case: Verify the pulse modulation settings for 380 to 2,700 MHz and 3,100 to 6,000 MHz.
requirements.why: This sets the disturbance the ESA must withstand in these bands.

requirements.text: The frequency step size and dwell time shall be chosen according to ISO 11452-1.
requirements.test_case: Check the step size and dwell time in the test report against ISO 11452-1.
requirements.why: This constrains the exposure duration applied to the ESA.

requirements.text: If the ESA fails the tests defined in Annex 9, it shall be verified as having failed under the relevant test conditions and not as a result of the generation of uncontrolled fields.
requirements.test_case: On any failure, check field calibration and monitoring data to exclude uncontrolled fields.
requirements.why: This governs how a failure of the lamp ESA is assessed.

requirements.text: For the absorber chamber test, the substitution method shall be used to establish the test field conditions according to ISO 11452-2.
requirements.test_case: Review the field calibration record for the substitution method.
requirements.why: This applies if the lamp ESA is tested in an absorber chamber.

requirements.text: The absorber chamber test shall be performed with vertical polarization.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the antenna orientation during the test.
requirements.why: This defines the exposure condition applied to the ESA.

requirements.text: TEM cell testing of the ESA shall be performed according to ISO 11452-3, with the method of maximum field coupling to the ESA or to the wiring harness inside the TEM cell.
requirements.test_case: Verify the TEM cell setup and coupling orientation against ISO 11452-3.
requirements.why: This applies if the lamp ESA is tested in a TEM cell.

requirements.text: Bulk current injection testing shall be performed according to ISO 11452-4 on a test bench, using either the substitution method with the injection probe positioned at 150 mm from the ESA or the closed loop method with the injection probe positioned at 900 mm from the ESA.
requirements.test_case: Measure the injection probe distance from the ESA and confirm the method used.
requirements.why: This applies if BCI is used for the lamp ESA.

requirements.text: Where the ESA is tested while installed in the vehicle, BCI testing shall be according to ISO 11451-4, using the substitution method with the injection probe positioned at 150 mm from the ESA.
requirements.test_case: Verify the in-vehicle BCI probe position of 150 mm and the substitution calibration.
requirements.why: This is the alternative BCI condition for the lamp ESA.

requirements.text: Stripline testing of the ESA shall be performed according to ISO 11452-5.
requirements.test_case: Audit the stripline setup against ISO 11452-5.
requirements.why: This applies if stripline testing is used for the lamp ESA.

requirements.text: Reverberation chamber testing of the ESA shall be performed according to ISO 11452-11 and, unless otherwise specified, using a test setup with ground plane.
requirements.test_case: Verify the reverberation chamber setup, including the ground plane, against ISO 11452-11.
requirements.why: This applies if reverberation chamber testing is used for the lamp ESA.

requirements.text: The ESA shall be immune to conducted transients on the vehicle power supply and shall limit conducted transients from the ESA to the vehicle power supply, as ensured by the test method of Annex 10.
requirements.test_case: Perform conducted transient immunity and emission tests per Annex 10 and verify both criteria are met.
requirements.why: The LED modules on PCB are an ESA connected to the 12/24 V vehicle supply.

requirements.text: The ESA shall withstand test pulses 1, 2a, 2b, 3a and 3b according to ISO 7637-2 applied to the supply lines as well as to other connections of the ESA which may be operationally connected to supply lines.
requirements.test_case: Apply ISO 7637-2 pulses 1, 2a, 2b, 3a and 3b to the lamp supply and connected lines and verify the functional status of the lamp functions.
requirements.why: The lamp ESA is powered from the 12/24 V supply lines and must show immunity to conducted transients.

requirements.text: The ESA, unless exclusively reserved for mounting on electric vehicles without 12V/24V starter motor, shall withstand the starting profile according to ISO 16750-2 applied to the supply lines as well as to other connections of the ESA which may be operationally connected to supply lines.
requirements.test_case: Apply the ISO 16750-2 starting profile to the lamp supply lines and verify the functional status of the lamp functions.
requirements.why: The M1 rear lamp ESA may be fitted to vehicles with a 12/24 V starter motor.

requirements.text: The emission of transient conducted disturbances generated by the ESA on 12/24 V supply lines, and on other connections of the ESA which may be operationally connected to supply lines, shall be measured according to ISO 7637-2.
requirements.test_case: Measure the conducted transient emission of the lamp on the supply lines per ISO 7637-2 and compare with the applicable limits.
requirements.why: The LED drive circuitry can generate transients on the vehicle supply lines.

requirements.text: The external surface of the vehicle (including the outer lens and housing of the rear lamp) shall not exhibit, directed outwards, any pointed or sharp parts or any projections of such shape, dimensions, direction or hardness as to be likely to increase the risk or seriousness of bodily injury to a person hit by the external surface or brushing against it in the event of a collision.
requirements.test_case: Visually and tactilely inspect the lamp as installed on the vehicle for outward-directed pointed or sharp parts or hazardous projections.
requirements.why: The outer lens and housing form part of the M1 vehicle's rear external surface.

requirements.text: The external surface of the vehicle (including the rear lamp outer lens and housing) shall not exhibit, directed outwards, any part likely to catch on pedestrians, cyclists or motor cyclists.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the installed lamp contour for outward-directed edges, hooks or gaps likely to catch on a person.
requirements.why: The lamp's exposed surfaces are part of the vehicle exterior subject to the catching prohibition.

requirements.text: No protruding part of the external surface (including the rear lamp outer lens and housing) shall have a radius of curvature less than 2.5 mm.
requirements.test_case: Measure radii of curvature of protruding lamp edges with radius gauges or a 3D scan, verifying ≥ 2.5 mm.
requirements.why: Protruding edges of the lens and housing are protruding parts of the external surface.

requirements.text: For parts of the external surface (including the rear lamp outer lens and housing) which protrude less than 5 mm, the 2.5 mm radius requirement does not apply, but the outward facing angles of such parts shall be blunted.
requirements.test_case: Measure the protrusion of lamp edges relative to the adjacent body; for those protruding between 1.5 mm and 5 mm, verify that the outward-facing angles are blunted.
requirements.why: Lamp edges with small protrusion relative to the body panel remain subject to the blunting requirement.

requirements.text: Parts of the external surface (including the rear lamp outer lens and housing) which protrude less than 1.5 mm are exempt from both the 2.5 mm radius requirement and the requirement to blunt outward facing angles.
requirements.test_case: Measure the protrusion height of lamp edges and confirm whether it is below 1.5 mm, which determines the exemption.
requirements.why: Sets the protrusion threshold that determines which lamp edges must meet the radius or blunting rules.

requirements.text: Where protruding parts of the external surface of the lamp (e.g. a seal or gasket) have a radius of curvature less than 2.5 mm on the grounds that they are made of a material of hardness not exceeding 60 Shore A, the hardness measurement shall be taken with the component as installed on the vehicle.
requirements.test_case: Measure the Shore A hardness of any soft protruding lamp component as installed on the vehicle and confirm it is ≤ 60 Shore A.
requirements.why: A TPE or silicone seal visible at the lamp periphery may rely on the soft-material exemption.

requirements.text: Where it is impossible to carry out a hardness measurement by the Shore A procedure on a protruding part of the lamp, comparable measurements shall be used for evaluation.
requirements.test_case: Where Shore A measurement is not feasible, apply an equivalent hardness method and document comparability.
requirements.why: Constrains how the soft-material exemption is demonstrated for lamp components.

requirements.text: The general provisions of paragraphs 5.1 to 5.5 shall apply to the rear lamp external surfaces in addition to the particular specifications of paragraph 6, except where those particular specifications expressly provide otherwise.
requirements.test_case: Check that the lamp design is assessed against both the paragraph 5 general rules and the applicable paragraph 6 particular rules for lamps.
requirements.why: Means the lamp must satisfy the general rules on top of the lamp-specific provisions of paragraph 6.

requirements.text: The vehicle (separate technical unit) carrying the rear lamp, approved under this Regulation, shall be so manufactured as to conform to the type approved by meeting the requirements set forth in paragraphs 5. and 6. (external projection requirements, including those applicable to the lamp's outer lens and housing surfaces).
requirements.test_case: Take series-production vehicles fitted with the lamp and re-check the external projections and radii of the lamp's outer surface against paragraphs 5 and 6 and the approved type.
requirements.why: The lamp forms part of the vehicle's external surface, so series production must keep complying with the R26 external-projection requirements.

requirements.text: For each type of product, at least the tests prescribed in Annex 3 to this Regulation (determination of projection height and dimensions of components mounted on the external surface) shall be carried out on production to verify conformity.
requirements.test_case: Measure the projection of the installed lamp on production vehicles using the 100 mm sphere / 165 mm circle method of Annex 3 and compare with the approved values.
requirements.why: The Annex 3 projection measurements on production units directly determine whether the lamp's outer surface remains compliant in series.

requirements.text: Any sample or test piece of the production showing non-conformity in the test considered shall give rise to another sampling and another test, and all necessary steps shall be taken to re-establish the conformity of the corresponding production.
requirements.test_case: Review CoP records to confirm that any failed projection measurement triggered resampling, retest and corrective action on the lamp/vehicle production.
requirements.why: A projection non-conformity found on series units fitted with the lamp must be retested and corrected before the product can continue to be supplied as conforming.

requirements.text: If the dimension of the projection of a component (lamp lens/housing) which is mounted on a surface other than convex cannot be determined by simple measurement, it shall be determined by the maximum variation of the distance of the centre of a 100 mm diameter sphere from the nominal line of the panel when the sphere is moved over and is in constant contact with that component.
requirements.test_case: Move a 100 mm diameter sphere over the installed rear lamp in constant contact and record the maximum variation of the sphere-centre distance from the nominal panel line; compare with the projection limits.
requirements.why: The rear lamp's outer lens and housing are external-surface components whose projection must be determined by this method when mounted on a non-convex surface.

requirements.text: The rear lamp (rear position, stop, reversing lamp and retro-reflector) shall be so fitted that under normal conditions of use and notwithstanding any vibrations to which it may be subjected, it retains the characteristics prescribed by UN R48 and enables the vehicle to comply with the requirements of the Regulation.
requirements.test_case: Vibration/durability test of the installed lamp followed by photometric and position re-check.
requirements.why: General installation obligation for all lighting and light-signalling devices fitted to the M1 vehicle.

requirements.text: It shall not be possible for the rear lamp to be inadvertently maladjusted.
requirements.test_case: Inspect mounting interface and fasteners for positive location with no adjustable or loose play.
requirements.why: Applies to all lamps installed on the vehicle including the rear combination lamp.

requirements.text: The reference axis of each light-signalling function of the rear lamp, when fitted to the vehicle, shall be parallel to the bearing plane of the vehicle on the road, with a tolerance of ±3°.
requirements.test_case: Measure reference axis inclination relative to the ground plane on the installed vehicle.
requirements.why: Applies to all light-signalling devices including rear position, stop and reversing lamps and rear retro-reflector.

requirements.text: The reference axis of the rear lamp functions (other than side retro-reflectors and side-marker lamps) shall be parallel to the median longitudinal plane of the vehicle, with a tolerance of ±3°.
requirements.test_case: Measure reference axis yaw relative to the vehicle median longitudinal plane.
requirements.why: Rear lamp functions are signalling devices other than side retro-reflectors/side-marker lamps.

requirements.text: Any specific instructions as regards fitting of the rear lamp laid down by the manufacturer shall be complied with.
requirements.test_case: Compare installation against manufacturer fitting instructions.
requirements.why: Installation condition binding the lamp fitment.

requirements.text: In the absence of specific instructions, the height and orientation of the rear lamps shall be verified with the vehicle unladen and placed on a flat, horizontal surface, in the normal condition of use.
requirements.test_case: Measure lamp height and orientation on unladen vehicle on flat horizontal surface.
requirements.why: Test condition constraining verification of the rear lamp position.

requirements.text: In the absence of specific instructions, rear lamps constituting a pair shall be fitted to the vehicle symmetrically in relation to the median longitudinal plane, based on the exterior geometrical form of the lamp and not on the edge of its illuminating surface.
requirements.test_case: Measure lateral positions of left and right lamps relative to vehicle centre plane.
requirements.why: Rear position, stop, reversing lamps and retro-reflectors are fitted as left/right pairs.

requirements.text: Rear lamps constituting a pair shall be symmetrical to one another in relation to the median longitudinal plane (not applicable to the interior structure of the lamp).
requirements.test_case: Compare exterior geometry of left and right lamps as mirror images.
requirements.why: Pair requirement for the left/right rear combination lamps.

requirements.text: Rear lamps constituting a pair shall satisfy the same colorimetric requirements.
requirements.test_case: Measure chromaticity of each function on left and right lamps.
requirements.why: Pair requirement for the rear lamp functions.

requirements.text: Rear lamps constituting a pair shall have substantially identical photometric characteristics.
requirements.test_case: Compare photometric measurements of left and right lamps.
requirements.why: Pair requirement for the rear lamp functions.

requirements.text: In case of rear lamps incorporating a manufacturer logo, only two lateral logos (one on each side) or one central logo can be fitted on the rear of the vehicle, and all logos that are not vehicle manufacturer or body manufacturer logos are prohibited.
requirements.test_case: Inspect lamp for logos and their number/position on the vehicle rear.
requirements.why: Applies if the rear lamp incorporates a logo.

requirements.text: On vehicles whose external shape is asymmetrical, the pair requirements of paragraph 5.5 shall be satisfied for the rear lamps so far as is possible.
requirements.test_case: Review symmetry of lamp installation on asymmetric body.
requirements.why: Conditional pair requirement for rear lamps.

requirements.text: Where the rear position, stop, reversing lamps and retro-reflector are grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated, all requirements regarding colour, position, orientation, geometric visibility, electrical connections and other requirements shall be fulfilled for each function.
requirements.test_case: Verify each function individually against its installation requirements.
requirements.why: The rear combination lamp groups several functions in one housing.

requirements.text: The photometric and colorimetric requirements of each rear lamp function shall be fulfilled when all other functions with which it is grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated are switched OFF.
requirements.test_case: Measure photometry and colour of each function with the other functions OFF.
requirements.why: Rear combination lamp has grouped/combined functions.

requirements.text: When the rear position lamp is reciprocally incorporated with one or more other functions (e.g. stop lamp) which can be switched ON together with it, the colour requirements of each of these other functions shall be fulfilled when the reciprocally incorporated function(s) and the rear position lamp are switched ON.
requirements.test_case: Measure stop lamp chromaticity with rear position lamp simultaneously ON.
requirements.why: Applies if rear position and stop functions share light-emitting surface.

requirements.text: The stop lamp shall not be reciprocally incorporated with a direction-indicator lamp.
requirements.test_case: Inspect design to confirm stop lamp does not share light source/surface with a direction indicator.
requirements.why: Design prohibition applying to the stop lamp function.

requirements.text: Where the apparent surface of a single lamp (rear position lamp, stop lamp or reversing lamp) is composed of two or more distinct parts, either the total area of the projection of the distinct parts in the direction of the reference axis on a plane tangent to the exterior surface of the outer lens and perpendicular to the reference axis shall occupy not less than 60 per cent of the smallest quadrilateral circumscribing that projection, or the minimum distance between the facing edges of two adjacent/tangential distinct parts shall not exceed 75 mm when measured perpendicularly to the reference axis.
requirements.test_case: Measure projected apparent surface parts and gap distances on the lamp drawing/sample.
requirements.why: The stop and position lamp sections consist of multiple distinct emitting parts (24 cups, 8 emitters).

requirements.text: The maximum height above the ground of each rear lamp function shall be measured from the highest point and the minimum height from the lowest point of the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis.
requirements.test_case: Measure height of apparent surface edges above ground on installed lamp.
requirements.why: Measurement rule constraining the lamp's mounting height compliance.

requirements.text: For the purposes of reducing the geometric visibility angles, the position of the rear lamp with regard to height above the ground shall be measured from the H plane.
requirements.test_case: Measure H-plane height of each function.
requirements.why: Determines applicability of reduced vertical visibility for the rear lamp.

requirements.text: The position of the rear lamp as regards width shall be determined from the edge of the apparent surface furthest from the median longitudinal plane when referred to the overall width, and from the inner edges of the apparent surface when referred to the distance between lamps.
requirements.test_case: Measure outer and inner edge positions of apparent surfaces.
requirements.why: Measurement rule for lateral position of rear lamp functions.

requirements.text: In the absence of specific instructions, the photometric characteristics (e.g. intensity, colour, apparent surface) of the rear position, stop and reversing lamps shall not be intentionally varied during the period when the lamp is switched ON.
requirements.test_case: Monitor intensity and colour over time with lamp ON.
requirements.why: General requirement for all lamps of the product.

requirements.text: Where the photometric characteristics of a rear lamp function vary in relation to the ambient light, as a consequence of other lamps being switched ON or OFF, or when the lamp is used to provide another lighting function, any variation shall be in compliance with the technical provisions for the lamp concerned.
requirements.test_case: Measure photometry of each function in all switching combinations.
requirements.why: Applies to combined/grouped functions such as position/stop.

requirements.text: Red light emitted by the rear position lamp, stop lamp and rear retro-reflector fitted on the rear of the vehicle shall not be visible from the front of the vehicle.
requirements.test_case: Check visibility of red apparent surfaces from the front observation zone.
requirements.why: Product emits red light at the rear of the vehicle.

requirements.text: There shall be no direct visibility of the apparent surface of the red rear lamps if viewed by an observer moving within Zone 1 in a transverse plane situated 25 m in front of the vehicle (bounded in height by 1 m and 2.2 m above ground and in width by planes at 15° outwards from the vehicle median plane through the vehicle's widest points).
requirements.test_case: Observer/sightline check in Zone 1 at 25 m in front of the vehicle.
requirements.why: Verification method for red-light-to-front prohibition applicable to the product.

requirements.text: In case of doubt, the luminous intensity of red light emitted to the front by the rear lamp shall not be more than 0.25 cd per lamp, taking into account the influence of the vehicle body if applicable.
requirements.test_case: Measure forward red luminous intensity of the lamp at type approval.
requirements.why: Quantitative limit for red light visible forward from the rear lamp.

requirements.text: The electrical connections shall be such that the rear position lamps can only be switched ON and OFF simultaneously with the front position lamps, end-outline marker lamps (if any), side-marker lamps (if any) and the rear registration plate lamp, except when used as parking lamps or under the other conditions of paragraph 5.11.1.
requirements.test_case: Functional switching test of the vehicle light circuit.
requirements.why: Electrical connection requirement for the rear position lamp function.

requirements.text: The rear position lamp, stop lamp, reversing lamp and rear retro-reflector shall not be concealed.
requirements.test_case: Inspect that no concealment device covers the lamp.
requirements.why: Concealment is prohibited for all lamps other than headlamps and front fog lamps.

requirements.text: The colour of the light emitted by the rear position lamp shall be red.
requirements.test_case: Colorimetric measurement of rear position lamp chromaticity.
requirements.why: Product contains a rear position lamp.

requirements.text: The colour of the light emitted by the stop lamp shall be red.
requirements.test_case: Colorimetric measurement of stop lamp chromaticity.
requirements.why: Product contains a stop lamp.

requirements.text: The colour of the light emitted by the reversing lamp shall be white.
requirements.test_case: Colorimetric measurement of reversing lamp chromaticity through its lens zone.
requirements.why: Product contains a reversing lamp (verify clear lens zone).

requirements.text: The colour of the rear retro-reflector, non-triangular, shall be red.
requirements.test_case: Colorimetric check of retro-reflector under CIE illuminant A.
requirements.why: Product contains a Class IA rear retro-reflector.

requirements.text: The number of rear position lamps, stop lamps, reversing lamps and rear retro-reflectors mounted on the vehicle shall be equal to the number indicated in the individual specifications of UN R48.
requirements.test_case: Count installed functions against paragraph 6 requirements.
requirements.why: Applies to each function provided by the product.

requirements.text: Where the rear position lamp or rear retro-reflector is installed on a movable component, at all fixed positions of the movable component the lamp shall meet all the position, geometric visibility, colorimetric and photometric requirements for those lamps.
requirements.test_case: Measure position, visibility and photometry at all fixed positions of the movable component.
requirements.why: Conditional on mounting the lamp on a tailgate/boot lid.

requirements.text: When movable components carrying the rear lamp are in a position other than a normal position of use, the lamp shall not cause undue discomfort to road users.
requirements.test_case: Assess glare/discomfort with movable component open.
requirements.why: Conditional on installation on a movable component.

requirements.text: When the rear lamp is installed on a movable component and the movable component is in the normal position(s) of use, the lamp shall always return to the position(s) specified by the manufacturer.
requirements.test_case: Cycle movable component and measure lamp position after return.
requirements.why: Conditional on installation on a movable component.

requirements.text: The apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis of the rear position lamps and rear retro-reflectors shall not be hidden more than 50 per cent by any movable component in any fixed position different from the normal position of use, otherwise additional lamps meeting all requirements shall be switched ON (or, for lamps other than retro-reflectors, the communication/notice provisions applied).
requirements.test_case: Measure hidden fraction of apparent surface with movable components in fixed open positions.
requirements.why: Applies to rear position lamps and retro-reflectors near movable components.

requirements.text: The rear position, stop and reversing lamps shall be capable of being made to operate by the sole installation of a light source and/or fuse; otherwise the lamp, even bearing an approval mark, is deemed not to be present.
requirements.test_case: Functional check that the lamp operates on installation without additional devices.
requirements.why: Defines effective presence of the product's lamp functions.

requirements.text: Where a temporary fail-safe replacement of the rear position lamp function is provided, the replacement function shall be similar in colour, main intensity and position to the function that has ceased to operate, the replacement device shall remain operational in its original safety function, and a tell-tale on the dashboard shall indicate occurrence of the temporary replacement and need for repair.
requirements.test_case: Simulate rear position lamp failure and verify replacement function and tell-tale.
requirements.why: Conditional on fail-safe replacement being implemented for the rear position lamp.

requirements.text: Where rear position lamps of category R2 and stop lamps of category S2 have variable luminous intensity control, the intensity of all such lamps when combined, grouped or reciprocally incorporated shall vary all together in the same manner and in a similar proportion.
requirements.test_case: Measure intensity of R2 and S2 functions across control range.
requirements.why: Conditional on variable-intensity rear position/stop lamps.

requirements.text: Where variable luminous intensity control is used, in the entire intensity range the specific prescribed ratio between the luminous intensities of two lamps (e.g. stop lamp to rear position lamp) shall be maintained throughout variation transitions.
requirements.test_case: Measure stop/position intensity ratio throughout transitions.
requirements.why: Conditional on variable-intensity rear position/stop lamps.

requirements.text: Increase and decrease of luminous intensity of variable-intensity rear position and stop lamps shall be within the limits prescribed in the pertinent UN Regulations and only in relation to ambient lighting, fog, snowfall, rain, spray, dust clouds or contamination of the light emitting surface.
requirements.test_case: Verify intensity limits under each triggering condition.
requirements.why: Conditional on variable-intensity R2/S2 functions.

requirements.text: A decrease of luminous intensity of variable-intensity rear position and stop lamps for traffic conditions shall be within the limits prescribed and only while vehicle speed is equal or less than 20 km/h or distance to the following vehicle is equal or less than 20 m; an activated decrease may remain active only as long as vehicle speed is equal or less than 50 km/h.
requirements.test_case: Vehicle test verifying intensity reduction thresholds at 20 km/h, 20 m and 50 km/h.
requirements.why: Conditional on variable-intensity R2/S2 functions.

requirements.text: No sharp variation of intensity shall be observed during transition of variable-intensity rear position and stop lamps.
requirements.test_case: Record intensity over time during transitions.
requirements.why: Conditional on variable-intensity R2/S2 functions.

requirements.text: For devices tested with a special power supply or at a voltage requested by the applicant, the voltage supplied at the terminals of the rear lamp shall not exceed the voltage specified for the relevant device or function as approved.
requirements.test_case: Measure terminal voltage in constant voltage vehicle operating condition.
requirements.why: Electric supply condition for M1 lamps not including electronic control gear.

requirements.text: In all other cases (where the lamp does not include an electronic light source control gear or variable intensity control), the voltage at the terminals of the rear lamp functions shall not exceed 13.5 V (12 Volt-Systems) or 28 V (24 Volt-Systems) by more than 3 per cent.
requirements.test_case: Measure lamp terminal voltage with vehicle electrical system at constant operating voltage.
requirements.why: Applies to the rear lamp unless its LED circuitry constitutes electronic control gear per 5.27.3.

requirements.text: There shall be no obstacle on the inside of the angles of geometric visibility to the propagation of light from any part of the apparent surface of each rear lamp function observed from infinity, unless the obstacle was already present when the lamp was type-approved.
requirements.test_case: Geometric visibility check of installed lamp over the prescribed angles.
requirements.why: General geometric visibility provision for the product's functions.

requirements.text: If any part of the apparent surface of the installed rear lamp is hidden by further parts of the vehicle, the part of the lamp not hidden shall still conform to the photometric values prescribed for the approval of the device.
requirements.test_case: Photometric measurement with masking representative of vehicle obstruction.
requirements.why: Applies to the installed rear lamp in a wraparound body-side position.

requirements.text: Where the rear lamp is mounted at less than 750 mm above the ground (measured from the H plane) and the vertical geometric visibility below horizontal is reduced to 5°, the photometric field of measurement of the installed optical unit may be reduced to 5° below the horizontal.
requirements.test_case: Check mounting height and corresponding photometric field.
requirements.why: Constrains photometric verification of the low-mounted rear lamp.

requirements.text: The rear position lamp, stop lamp, reversing lamp and rear retro-reflector shall be type approved according to the corresponding device Regulations as specified in paragraph 6 of UN R48 when installed on a vehicle.
requirements.test_case: Verify device approval marks (e.g. UN R148, R150) on the lamp.
requirements.why: Each function of the product requires device type approval.

requirements.text: Where the rear lamp incorporates a manufacturer logo, the lamp shall be type approved according to the requirements of UN Regulation No. 148.
requirements.test_case: Check R148 approval covering logo.
requirements.why: Conditional on logo integration in the light-signalling lamp.

requirements.text: The reversing lamp shall be present (mandatory) on motor vehicles.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the vehicle installation to confirm a reversing lamp is fitted.
requirements.why: The product provides the reversing lamp function for an M1 motor vehicle, where it is mandatory.

requirements.text: For motor vehicles of category M1, one reversing lamp device shall be mandatory and a second device is optional.
requirements.test_case: Count the reversing lamp devices installed on the M1 vehicle (1 or 2).
requirements.why: The product is the M1 reversing lamp device and determines the number of devices fitted.

requirements.text: The reversing lamp devices shall be type-approved according to the 00 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 23, or to the 00 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 148.
requirements.test_case: Check the approval marking on the lamp for R23 or R148 approval.
requirements.why: P-03 reversing lamp must carry a component type approval to be installed.

requirements.text: The reversing lamp shall be positioned in height not less than 250 mm and not more than 1,200 mm above the ground.
requirements.test_case: Measure the height of the reversing lamp illuminating surface above the ground on the vehicle in unladen condition.
requirements.why: Installation height applies to the reversing lamp in the product's mounting position.

requirements.text: The reversing lamp shall be positioned in length at the rear of the vehicle.
requirements.test_case: Inspect that the reversing lamp is installed at the rear of the vehicle.
requirements.why: The rear lamp is rear-mounted and carries the reversing function.

requirements.text: For reversing lamps installed at the rear of the vehicle, the vertical angles of geometric visibility shall be α = 15° upwards and 5° downwards.
requirements.test_case: Verify visibility of the apparent surface over the vertical angular field 15° up and 5° down.
requirements.why: Geometric visibility applies to the rear-mounted reversing lamp.

requirements.text: For reversing lamps installed at the rear of the vehicle, where there is only one device, the horizontal angle of geometric visibility shall be β = 45° to the right and to the left.
requirements.test_case: Verify visibility of the apparent surface over 45° left and right for a single-device installation.
requirements.why: Applies to an M1 installation with one reversing lamp.

requirements.text: For reversing lamps installed at the rear of the vehicle, where there are two devices, the horizontal angle of geometric visibility shall be β = 45° outwards and 30° inwards.
requirements.test_case: Verify visibility of the apparent surface over 45° outwards and 30° inwards for each lamp of a two-device installation.
requirements.why: Applies when the optional second reversing lamp is fitted on the M1 vehicle.

requirements.text: The reversing lamp shall be oriented rearwards.
requirements.test_case: Inspect that the reference axis of the reversing lamp is directed rearwards.
requirements.why: Orientation requirement applies to the installed reversing lamp.

requirements.text: The electrical connections shall be such that the reversing lamp can be switched ON only if the reverse gear is engaged and if the device which controls the starting and stopping of the propulsion system is in such a position that operation of the propulsion system is possible.
requirements.test_case: Functional test: engage reverse gear with propulsion system operable and confirm the lamp lights; check it cannot be lit otherwise.
requirements.why: Electrical connection rule governs activation of the product's reversing function.

requirements.text: The reversing lamp shall not switch ON or remain ON if either the reverse gear is not engaged or the device which controls the starting and stopping of the propulsion system is not in a position where operation of the propulsion system is possible.
requirements.test_case: Functional test: disengage reverse or switch off propulsion and confirm the lamp extinguishes and cannot be switched on.
requirements.why: Electrical connection rule governs deactivation of the product's reversing function.

requirements.text: A tell-tale indicating failure of the reversing lamp shall be provided if required by the component regulation.
requirements.test_case: Check the component regulation (R23/R148) requirement and, if applicable, simulate a lamp failure and verify the tell-tale activates.
requirements.why: Failure tell-tale may be mandated for the product's reversing lamp via its component regulation.

requirements.text: Stop lamp devices of S1 or S2 categories shall be present (mandatory) on all categories of vehicles, including M1.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the vehicle installation to confirm S1/S2 stop lamps are fitted.
requirements.why: P-02 is a rear-mounted stop lamp on an M1 vehicle, i.e. an S1/S2 category device.

requirements.text: The number of S1 or S2 category stop lamp devices shall be two.
requirements.test_case: Count the S1/S2 stop lamps installed on the vehicle (left and right rear lamps).
requirements.why: The rear lamp provides one of the two mandatory S1/S2 stop lamps.

requirements.text: The stop lamp devices shall be type-approved according to the 02 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 7, or to the 00 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 148.
requirements.test_case: Check that the stop lamp bears a valid R7 (02 series or later) or R148 approval marking.
requirements.why: P-02 stop lamp must carry device approval to be installed.

requirements.text: For M1 category vehicles, the point on the apparent surface of the S1 or S2 category stop lamp in the direction of the reference axis which is farthest from the vehicle's median longitudinal plane shall not be more than 400 mm from the extreme outer edge of the vehicle.
requirements.test_case: Measure the lateral distance from the outermost point of the stop lamp apparent surface to the vehicle's extreme outer edge (≤ 400 mm).
requirements.why: Width position constraint for S1/S2 stop lamps on M1 vehicles.

requirements.text: The S1 or S2 category stop lamp shall be positioned above the ground not less than 350 mm nor more than 1,500 mm (2,100 mm if the shape of the bodywork makes it impossible to keep within 1,500 mm and if the optional lamps are not installed).
requirements.test_case: Measure the height of the lower and upper edges of the apparent surface above ground in the unladen vehicle condition.
requirements.why: Height position constraint for the S1/S2 stop lamp function of the rear lamp.

requirements.text: The S1 or S2 category stop lamp shall be positioned, in length, at the rear of the vehicle.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the installation to confirm the stop lamp is mounted at the rear of the vehicle.
requirements.why: Longitudinal position requirement for S1/S2 stop lamps.

requirements.text: The geometric visibility horizontal angle for S1 or S2 category stop lamps shall be 45° to the left and to the right of the longitudinal axis of the vehicle.
requirements.test_case: Verify the unobstructed apparent surface visibility over ±45° horizontally on the vehicle.
requirements.why: Geometric visibility requirement for the S1/S2 stop lamp.

requirements.text: For stop lamps of categories S1 and S2 mounted below 750 mm (measured from the H plane according to paragraph 5.8.1.), the inward horizontal angle of 45° may be reduced to 20° under the H plane.
requirements.test_case: Where the lamp is below 750 mm, verify inward visibility of at least 20° below the H plane.
requirements.why: Defines the minimum visibility angle applicable if the stop lamp is mounted low.

requirements.text: The geometric visibility vertical angle for S1 or S2 category stop lamps shall be 15° above and below the horizontal.
requirements.test_case: Verify unobstructed visibility of the apparent surface over ±15° vertically.
requirements.why: Geometric visibility requirement for the S1/S2 stop lamp.

requirements.text: Where an S1 or S2 stop lamp is mounted below 750 mm (measured from the H plane according to paragraph 5.8.1.), the downward vertical angle of 15° may be reduced to 5°.
requirements.test_case: Where the lamp is mounted below 750 mm, verify downward visibility of at least 5°.
