requirements.why: It applies if the LED modules are replaceable light source modules.

requirements.text: In case replaceable light source module(s) is/are used, the lamp shall bear the specific identification code of the module and the rated voltage(s) or the range of voltage.
requirements.test_case: If replaceable modules are used, inspect the lamp for the module MD code and voltage.
requirements.why: It applies if the LED modules are replaceable light source modules.

requirements.text: An electronic light source control gear or variable luminous intensity control being part of the lamp, but not included into the lamp body, shall be marked with its identification number and the name of the manufacturer.
requirements.test_case: If an external control gear exists, inspect it for the ID number and manufacturer name.
requirements.why: The LED lamp may use separate control electronics.

requirements.text: The approval marking shall be placed on an inner or outer part (transparent or not) of the lamp which is not designed to be separated from the transparent part of the lamp emitting the light.
requirements.test_case: Verify the marking location is on the lens or on a part permanently joined to the lens.
requirements.why: This sets the marking location requirement for the lamp.

requirements.text: The approval marking, as well as the category or categories of LED substitute light source(s) prescribed if any, shall be visible when the lamp is fitted on the vehicle or when a movable part such as the hood or boot lid or a door is opened.
requirements.test_case: Check marking visibility with the lamp installed on the vehicle (with the boot lid opened if necessary).
requirements.why: This is a visibility requirement for the lamp's approval marking.

requirements.text: If the outer lens of the device is designed to be separated from the main body, the approval marking shall be placed on both the detachable lens and the main body.
requirements.test_case: If the lens is detachable, verify markings exist on both the lens and the housing.
requirements.why: The outer lens is a part of this lamp.

requirements.text: In case an outer lens is used for several devices and bears different approval markings, the main body of each device shall bear only the approval marking of the function(s) of that device.
requirements.test_case: If a common lens is used, inspect each main body for only its own function markings.
requirements.why: The outer lens covers several functions of the lamp.

requirements.text: The approval marking and the markings in paragraphs 3.3.3.2, 3.3.3.3, 3.3.3.4, 3.3.3.5 (b) and 3.3.3.6 shall be affixed on the lamp.
requirements.test_case: Inspect that these markings are on the lamp itself.
requirements.why: This defines where the lamp's markings must be applied.

requirements.text: The markings in paragraph 3.3.3.5 (a) shall be affixed on the light source module component.
requirements.test_case: If replaceable modules are used, verify the module markings are on the module.
requirements.why: It applies if replaceable light source modules are used.

requirements.text: Where a single approval mark is affixed to grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps, it shall be visible after their installation.
requirements.test_case: With the lamp installed, check the single approval mark is visible.
requirements.why: The rear combination lamp groups the position, stop and reversing lamps and the retro-reflector.

requirements.text: Where a single approval mark is affixed to grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps, no part of the lamps that transmits light can be removed without at the same time removing the approval mark.
requirements.test_case: Verify that removing any light-transmitting part necessarily removes the mark.
requirements.why: This applies to the grouped rear combination lamp.

requirements.text: The size of the components of a single approval mark shall not be less than the minimum size required for the smallest of the individual marks by the pertinent UN Regulations under which approval has been granted.
requirements.test_case: Measure the mark components against the minimum sizes of R148 and R150.
requirements.why: This applies to a single mark covering the R148 lamps and the R150 retro-reflector.

requirements.text: Each lamp (rear position lamp, stop lamp, reversing lamp) submitted for approval shall conform to the requirements set forth in paragraphs 4. and 5.
requirements.test_case: Review the type-approval test report for full compliance with paragraphs 4 and 5 for each function.
requirements.why: Applies to every lamp approved under R148, including all three functions of this rear lamp.

requirements.text: The requirements of sections 5 'General specifications' and 6 'Individual specifications' of UN Regulation No. 48 (and referenced Annexes) pertinent to each lamp and to vehicle category M1 shall be applied to the lamp where their verification at the moment of lamp type approval is feasible.
requirements.test_case: Check the lamp against the applicable R48 installation provisions (e.g. geometric visibility, colour) verifiable on the device.
requirements.why: The lamp is intended for M1 vehicles, so the relevant R48 provisions are imported into its approval.

requirements.text: The lamps shall be so designed and constructed that in normal conditions of use, and notwithstanding the vibrations to which they may be subjected in such use, their satisfactory operation remains assured and they retain the characteristics prescribed by this Regulation.
requirements.test_case: Perform vibration/durability testing, then re-verify photometry and colour.
requirements.why: General design requirement for all lamps.

requirements.text: In the case of a rear position lamp reciprocally incorporated with a stop lamp, these functions shall either (a) be provided by multiple light sources, or (b) be intended for use in a vehicle equipped with a tell-tale indicating failure for the lamps.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the circuit/LED layout for separate light sources for position and stop, or confirm the failure tell-tale signal and the note in the communication form.
requirements.why: The rear position and stop functions may share the LED/reflector array (reciprocal incorporation).

requirements.text: Where a manufacturer logo is incorporated in the optical components or outer lens texture inside the apparent surface, only the logo of the brand name of the vehicle manufacturer or the body manufacturer is allowed.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the lens/optics for logos and verify the logo against the manufacturer statement.
requirements.why: The outer lens of a rear position lamp may incorporate a logo.

requirements.text: Where a logo is incorporated, the enclosed light emitting surface of the logo (incorporating transparent and non-transparent components) in the direction of the reference axis shall not exceed 100 cm2.
requirements.test_case: Measure the projected logo light-emitting area in the reference-axis direction.
requirements.why: Limits logo size on the rear position lamp function.

requirements.text: Stop lamps and reversing lamps shall not incorporate a logo.
requirements.test_case: Visually inspect the stop and reversing lamp apparent surfaces for any logo.
requirements.why: The product includes stop and reversing lamp functions.

requirements.text: In a single lamp containing more than one light source, a group of light sources wired so that the failure of any one of them causes all of them to stop emitting light shall be considered to be one light source.
requirements.test_case: Analyse the LED wiring topology to identify light-source groups.
requirements.why: The LED modules contain multiple LEDs per function.

requirements.text: In case of failure of any one light source in a single lamp containing more than one light source, either (a) the light intensity shall comply with the minimum intensity required in the pertinent standard light distribution table of Annex 3, with maximum intensities not exceeded when all light sources are illuminated, or (b) a signal for activation of a tell-tale indicating failure according to UN Regulation No. 48 shall be produced.
requirements.test_case: Disable each light source in turn and measure photometry against the minima, or verify that the failure signal is generated.
requirements.why: The rear position, stop and reversing functions use multiple LEDs.

requirements.text: In case of failure of the variable intensity control of a rear position lamp of category R2 emitting more than the maximum value of category R1, the requirements of steady luminous intensity of category R1 shall be fulfilled automatically.
requirements.test_case: Simulate a variable intensity control failure and measure that intensities fall within R1 steady values.
requirements.why: Applies if the rear position lamp is category R2 with variable intensity.

requirements.text: In case of failure of the variable intensity control of a stop lamp of category S2 emitting more than the maximum value of category S1, the requirements of steady luminous intensity of category S1 shall be fulfilled automatically.
requirements.test_case: Simulate a variable intensity control failure and measure that intensities fall within S1 steady values.
requirements.why: Applies if the stop lamp is category S2 with variable intensity.

requirements.text: The lamp shall only be equipped with replaceable light source(s) approved according to UN Regulations Nos. 37, 99 and/or 128, and/or light source module(s), and/or non-replaceable light source(s).
requirements.test_case: Inspect the light-source type and its approval status.
requirements.why: The lamp uses LED modules on PCB as light sources.

requirements.text: Light signalling devices shall not generate radiated or power line disturbances which cause a malfunction of other electric/electronic systems of the vehicle.
requirements.test_case: Perform EMC emission tests (radiated and conducted) on the lamp and its LED driver.
requirements.why: The lamp contains LED electronics on a PCB.

requirements.text: In case of replaceable light source module(s), the light source module shall only be fitted in the designated and correct position and shall only be removable with the use of tool(s).
requirements.test_case: Attempt incorrect fitting and tool-less removal of the module.
requirements.why: Applies if the LED modules are replaceable light source modules (replaceability unconfirmed).

requirements.text: In case of replaceable light source module(s), the light source module shall be tamperproof.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the module design for tamper resistance.
requirements.why: Applies if the LED modules are replaceable light source modules.

requirements.text: In case of replaceable light source module(s), regardless of the use of tool(s), the module shall not be interchangeable with any replaceable UN approved light source or with any other replaceable light source module having different characteristics located in the same lamp housing.
requirements.test_case: Attempt cross-fitting of modules between functions and with standard light sources.
requirements.why: Applies if the position, stop and reversing modules are replaceable within the same housing.

requirements.text: In case of replaceable light source module(s), when the module is removed and replaced by another module provided by the applicant and bearing the same light source module identification code, the photometric requirements of the device shall be met.
requirements.test_case: Swap the module for another with the same identification code and re-measure photometry.
requirements.why: Applies if the LED modules are replaceable.

requirements.text: For a lamp equipped with light source module(s) or non-replaceable light source(s), all photometric and colorimetric measurements shall be made with the light source(s) present in the lamp.
requirements.test_case: Perform the photometric/colorimetric measurement with the production LED modules installed.
requirements.why: The lamp uses LED modules or non-replaceable LEDs.

requirements.text: During photometric measurements, stray reflections shall be avoided by appropriate masking.
requirements.test_case: Verify that masking is applied in the goniophotometer setup.
requirements.why: This test condition constrains the photometric verification of the lamp.

requirements.text: Where the lamp may be installed on the vehicle in more than one position or in a field of different positions, the photometric measurements shall be repeated for each position or for the extreme positions of the field of the reference axis specified by the manufacturer.
requirements.test_case: Measure photometry at each declared mounting position or at the extreme positions.
requirements.why: Applies if the body-side lamp is declared for several mounting orientations.

requirements.text: If not otherwise specified, the intensities shall be measured with the light source continuously lit.
requirements.test_case: Run photometry with the LEDs in steady operation.
requirements.why: Measurement condition for the position, stop and reversing functions.

requirements.text: Where measurement results are challenged, the distance of measurement shall be such that the law of the inverse of the square of the distance is applicable.
requirements.test_case: Verify the photometric distance is sufficient for the inverse-square law to apply.
requirements.why: Defines valid measurement of the lamp intensities in case of dispute.

requirements.text: Where measurement results are challenged, the angular aperture of the receiver viewed from the reference centre of the light shall be between 10' and 1 degree.
requirements.test_case: Check the receiver aperture geometry.
requirements.why: Defines valid measurement of the lamp intensities in case of dispute.

requirements.text: The intensity requirement for a particular direction of observation shall be deemed satisfied if it is met in a direction deviating by not more than one-quarter of a degree from the direction of observation.
requirements.test_case: Evaluate any marginal test points within ±0.25° of the nominal direction.
requirements.why: Pass criterion for the lamp intensities.

requirements.text: The limits of the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis of each light-signalling lamp (rear position, stop, reversing) shall be determined.
requirements.test_case: Determine and document the apparent surface outline on the drawings for each function.
requirements.why: The product is a light-signalling lamp.

requirements.text: Unless otherwise specified, the voltage supplied at the lamp for testing shall be 13.5 V for 12 Volt systems (6.75 V for 6 V systems, 28 V for 24 V systems).
requirements.test_case: Supply 13.5 V at the lamp connector during photometric tests.
requirements.why: Test condition for the lamp's photometric compliance.

requirements.text: For a lamp controlled by an electronic light source control gear or a variable intensity control, the lamp shall be operated as specified by the applicant.
requirements.test_case: Operate the lamp with the declared control gear and settings.
requirements.why: Applies if the LED modules use driver electronics or variable intensity control.

requirements.text: For a lamp with light source module(s) or non-replaceable light source(s) not controlled by an electronic light source control gear or a variable intensity control, the lamp shall be operated as specified by the applicant.
requirements.test_case: Operate the lamp under the declared electrical conditions.
requirements.why: The lamp uses LED modules or non-replaceable light sources.

requirements.text: The intensity of light emitted by each of the two samples shall, on the reference axis (HV), be not less than the minimum specified in the table of the pertinent function in paragraph 5.
requirements.test_case: Measure HV intensity for the position, stop and reversing functions on both samples.
requirements.why: Photometric minimum for each function of the lamp.

requirements.text: The intensity of light emitted by each of the two samples shall, in no direction where the lamp is visible, exceed the maximum specified in the table of the pertinent function in paragraph 5.
requirements.test_case: Perform a goniophotometric scan to find the maximum intensity per function.
requirements.why: Photometric maximum for each function of the lamp.

requirements.text: Outside the reference axis, the intensity shall be not less than the product of the minimum specified in paragraph 5 by the percentage specified in the pertinent light distribution figure of Annex 3, or not less than the intensity value specified in that figure (in cd for reversing lamps), for each direction in question.
requirements.test_case: Measure the Annex 3 grid points (Figure A3-I for position/stop, A3-V for reversing).
requirements.why: Light distribution requirement for each function.

requirements.text: Within the angles of geometric visibility defined in the tables in Annex 2, the intensity shall be not less than the minimum specified in the table of the pertinent function in paragraph 5, and the provisions of Annex 3 on local variations of intensity shall be observed.
requirements.test_case: Measure across the Annex 2 visibility angles and check uniformity between grid points.
requirements.why: Geometric visibility requirement for the position and stop functions.

requirements.text: An interdependent lamp system shall meet the requirements when all its interdependent lamps are operated together.
requirements.test_case: Measure the photometry with all interdependent lamps lit together.
requirements.why: Applies if the rear position/stop functions are approved as a 'Y' interdependent system.

requirements.text: The variable intensity control shall not generate signals which cause luminous intensities outside the range specified in paragraph 5.
requirements.test_case: Sweep the control inputs and measure that intensities stay within the paragraph 5 range.
requirements.why: Applies if the position/stop lamp has variable intensity control.

requirements.text: The variable intensity control shall not generate signals which cause luminous intensities exceeding the steady luminous intensity maximum specified in paragraph 5, under night-time conditions for systems depending only on daytime and night-time conditions, or under standard conditions for other systems.
requirements.test_case: Measure maximum intensity under night-time or standard conditions with the control active.
requirements.why: Applies if the position/stop lamp has variable intensity control.

requirements.text: If the rear position lamp is reciprocally incorporated with the stop lamp, the ratio between the luminous intensities of the two lamps when turned on simultaneously and of the rear position lamp turned on alone shall be at least 5:1 in the field bounded by ±5° V and ±10° H, with all light sources in operation where a lamp contains more than one light source considered as a single lamp.
requirements.test_case: Measure position-only and position+stop intensities across ±10° H/±5° V and compute the ratio.
requirements.why: The position and stop functions may be reciprocally incorporated.

requirements.text: Tests for compliance of the luminous intensities shall be carried out according to Annex 8 (for LED functions: compliance after 1 min and after 30 min or photometric stability for position and stop lamps; after 1 min and 10 min for reversing lamps).
requirements.test_case: Perform time-dependent photometry per Annex 8 for each function.
requirements.why: Defines the photometric compliance timing for the LED functions.

requirements.text: The colour of the light emitted shall be measured inside the field of the light distribution grid defined for the specific function in Annex 3, with the light sources present in the lamp, and shall comply with the colour prescribed for the function (red for rear position and stop lamps, white for the reversing lamp).
requirements.test_case: Perform a spectroradiometric colour measurement across the Annex 3 grid for each function.
requirements.why: Colour requirement for the red and white functions; the lens tint must suit each function.

requirements.text: Outside the field of the light distribution grid, no sharp variation of colour shall be observed.
requirements.test_case: Visually or colorimetrically inspect the colour outside the grid field.
requirements.why: Colour uniformity requirement for each lamp function.

requirements.text: The light emitted by each of the two samples of the rear position lamp supplied shall meet the luminous intensity and standard light distribution requirements in Table 4.
requirements.test_case: Goniophotometric measurement of both samples against Table 4 values.
requirements.why: P-01 is a rear position lamp, and 5.2.1 sets its photometric requirements.

requirements.text: For rear position lamps reciprocally incorporated with stop lamps, a luminous intensity of up to 6.0∙10^1 cd shall be permitted below a plane forming an angle of 5° with and downward from the horizontal plane; elsewhere the Table 4 maximum applies.
requirements.test_case: With the position and stop functions reciprocally incorporated, measure the position-lamp intensity below 5° down and check it is ≤ 60 cd.
requirements.why: The position and stop functions may share emitters or reflector cups in this combination lamp.

requirements.text: For a rear position lamp of category R1 (steady), the minimum luminous intensity (in the reference axis) shall be 4∙10^0 cd.
requirements.test_case: Measure the intensity on the reference axis and check it is ≥ 4 cd.
requirements.why: This limit applies if the position lamp is approved as R1.

requirements.text: For a rear position lamp of category R1 (steady), the maximum luminous intensity shall be 1.7∙10^1 cd when used as a single lamp, and 8.5∙10^0 cd for a lamp marked "D".
requirements.test_case: Measure the maximum intensity over the light distribution and compare it with 17 cd (single lamp) or 8.5 cd (marked "D").
requirements.why: This limit applies if the position lamp is approved as R1.

requirements.text: For a rear position lamp of category R2 (variable), the minimum luminous intensity shall be 4∙10^0 cd.
requirements.test_case: Measure the intensity on the reference axis and check it is ≥ 4 cd.
requirements.why: This limit applies if the position lamp is approved as R2 (variable intensity).

requirements.text: For a rear position lamp of category R2 (variable), the maximum luminous intensity shall be 4.2∙10^1 cd when used as a single lamp, and 2.1∙10^1 cd for a lamp marked "D".
requirements.test_case: Measure the maximum intensity and compare it with 42 cd (single lamp) or 21 cd (marked "D").
requirements.why: This limit applies if the position lamp is approved as R2.

requirements.text: The rear position lamp shall conform to the standard light distribution of Figure A3-I.
requirements.test_case: Measure the intensities at the Figure A3-I grid points and check each against its required percentage of the minimum.
requirements.why: Table 4 specifies this light distribution for R1 and R2 lamps.

requirements.text: Within the angles of geometric visibility defined in Table A2-1, the rear position lamp shall provide a minimum luminous intensity of 5∙10^-2 cd.
requirements.test_case: Measure the intensity at the boundaries of the Table A2-1 geometric visibility angles and check it is ≥ 0.05 cd.
requirements.why: 5.2.2 and Table 4 set the minimum intensity within the visibility angles for rear position lamps.

requirements.text: The rear position lamp shall comply with the failure provisions of paragraph 4.6.
requirements.test_case: Simulate failure of LEDs or circuit elements and verify behaviour against paragraph 4.6.
requirements.why: The LED multi-source position lamp falls under the failure provisions.

requirements.text: The colour of light emitted by the rear position lamp shall be red.
requirements.test_case: Measure the chromaticity coordinates through the outer lens and check they fall within the red colour boundaries.
requirements.why: 5.2.7 requires the position lamp to emit red light.

requirements.text: The light emitted by each of the two samples of the stop lamp supplied shall meet the luminous intensity and standard light distribution requirements in Table 7.
requirements.test_case: Goniophotometric measurement of both samples against the Table 7 values for the declared category.
requirements.why: P-02 is a stop lamp, and 5.5.1 sets its photometric performance.

requirements.text: For a stop lamp of category S1 (steady), the luminous intensity shall be minimum 6.0∙10^1 cd and maximum 2.60∙10^2 cd for a single lamp, or maximum 1.30∙10^2 cd for a lamp marked "D".
requirements.test_case: Measure the intensity in the reference axis and check it lies between the minimum and the applicable maximum.
requirements.why: The M1 body-mounted rear stop lamp is category S1 or S2.

requirements.text: For a stop lamp of category S1 (steady), the standard light distribution shall comply with Figure A3-I.
requirements.test_case: Measure the intensities at the Figure A3-I grid points and compare them with the required percentages.
requirements.why: This is the light distribution requirement for an S1 stop lamp.

requirements.text: For a stop lamp of category S1 (steady), the minimum luminous intensity within the angles of geometric visibility defined in Table A2-1 shall be 3∙10^-1 cd.
requirements.test_case: Measure the intensity across the Table A2-1 visibility angles and verify it is ≥0.3 cd.
requirements.why: This is the visibility requirement for an S1 stop lamp.

requirements.text: For a stop lamp of category S2 (variable), the luminous intensity shall be minimum 6.0∙10^1 cd and maximum 7.30∙10^2 cd for a single lamp, or maximum 3.65∙10^2 cd for a lamp marked "D".
requirements.test_case: Measure the intensity under the variable-intensity operating conditions and check the min/max limits.
requirements.why: This applies if the stop lamp is a variable-intensity S2 lamp.

requirements.text: For a stop lamp of category S2 (variable), the standard light distribution shall comply with Figure A3-I.
requirements.test_case: Measure the intensities at the Figure A3-I grid points and compare them with the required percentages.
requirements.why: This is the light distribution requirement for an S2 stop lamp.

requirements.text: For a stop lamp of category S2 (variable), the minimum luminous intensity within the angles of geometric visibility defined in Table A2-1 shall be 3∙10^-1 cd (day) and 7∙10^-2 cd (night).
requirements.test_case: Measure the intensity across the visibility angles in day and night modes and verify ≥0.3 cd and ≥0.07 cd respectively.
requirements.why: This is the visibility requirement for an S2 stop lamp.

requirements.text: The stop lamp shall meet the minimum luminous intensity within the angles of geometric visibility given in Table 7.
requirements.test_case: Photometric check of the minimum intensity over the full geometric visibility field.
requirements.why: 5.5.2 explicitly applies the geometric visibility minimum to the stop lamp.

requirements.text: The stop lamp shall comply with the failure provisions of paragraph 4.6.
requirements.test_case: Simulate LED failure and verify behaviour per paragraph 4.6.
requirements.why: P-02 uses multiple LEDs, so the failure provisions apply.

requirements.text: The colour of light emitted by the stop lamp shall be red.
requirements.test_case: Measure chromaticity coordinates with a spectroradiometer and verify they fall within the red boundaries.
requirements.why: 5.5.7 sets the colour requirement for the stop lamp.

requirements.text: The light emitted by each of the two samples of the reversing lamp shall meet the requirements in Table 10.
requirements.test_case: Goniophotometric measurement of both samples against Table 10 values.
requirements.why: P-03 is a reversing lamp of category AR approved under R148.

requirements.text: The reversing lamp (category AR) shall have a minimum luminous intensity of 8.0∙10^1 cd (Par. 4.8.3.1. (a)).
requirements.test_case: Measure luminous intensity at the reference axis and verify ≥ 80 cd.
requirements.why: Table 10 minimum intensity row for AR applies to P-03.

requirements.text: The reversing lamp (category AR) shall not exceed a maximum luminous intensity of 3.00∙10^2 cd in or above the h-plane.
requirements.test_case: Goniophotometric scan in and above the H-plane; verify all values ≤ 300 cd.
requirements.why: Table 10 maximum intensity limit for AR applies to P-03.

requirements.text: The reversing lamp (category AR) shall not exceed a maximum luminous intensity of 6.00∙10^2 cd below the h-plane down to 5°D.
requirements.test_case: Goniophotometric scan between H-plane and 5°D; verify all values ≤ 600 cd.
requirements.why: Table 10 maximum intensity limit for AR applies to P-03.

requirements.text: The reversing lamp (category AR) shall not exceed a maximum luminous intensity of 8.00∙10^3 cd below 5°D.
requirements.test_case: Goniophotometric scan below 5°D; verify all values ≤ 8000 cd.
requirements.why: Table 10 maximum intensity limit for AR applies to P-03.

requirements.text: The reversing lamp (category AR) shall comply with the standard light distribution of Figure A3-V (Par. 4.8.3.1. (c)).
requirements.test_case: Measure intensities at the Figure A3-V grid points and compare with the required percentages of minimum.
requirements.why: Table 10 standard light distribution requirement for AR applies to P-03.

requirements.text: Where the reversing lamp is intended to be installed on a vehicle exclusively in a pair of devices and photometry is verified only up to an angle of 30° inwards, a photometric value of at least 2.5∙10^1 cd shall be satisfied at that angle.
requirements.test_case: Measure luminous intensity at 30° inwards and verify ≥ 25 cd.
requirements.why: Conditional photometric requirement if P-03 is approved for pair-only installation.

requirements.text: Where type approval is granted with photometry verified only up to 30° inwards, the reversing lamp shall only be installed on a vehicle as part of a pair.
requirements.test_case: Check communication form item 9.1.3 and vehicle installation for pair mounting.
requirements.why: Installation restriction binding the lamp approved under the pair-only condition.

requirements.text: The reversing lamp shall comply with the failure provisions of paragraph 4.6.
requirements.test_case: Apply failure provisions of paragraph 4.6 (e.g. single LED failure test) and verify compliance.
requirements.why: Failure provisions apply to P-03 multi-LED reversing lamp.

requirements.text: The colour of light emitted by the reversing lamp shall be white.
requirements.test_case: Measure chromaticity coordinates of reversing lamp output and verify within white boundaries; check lens zone is not red-tinted.
requirements.why: Colour requirement for the reversing lamp function of P-03 and lens P-04.

requirements.text: Lamps (rear position lamp, stop lamp, reversing lamp) shall be so manufactured as to conform to the type approved under this Regulation.
requirements.test_case: Compare production samples against the approved type documentation and test report.
requirements.why: General CoP obligation applying to all R148 lamps in the product.

requirements.text: The compliance of production lamps with the requirements set forth in paragraph 5 shall be verified according to paragraphs 6.1.1 to 6.1.3.
requirements.test_case: Audit the CoP plan for coverage of paragraph 5 requirements.
requirements.why: Production lamps must keep meeting paragraph 5 technical requirements.

requirements.text: The minimum requirements for conformity of production control procedures set forth in Annex 4 shall be complied with for the lamps.
requirements.test_case: Audit the manufacturer's CoP procedures (photometric and colorimetric tests at appropriate intervals) against Annex 4.
requirements.why: Annex 4 CoP control applies to every R148 lamp type produced.

requirements.text: The minimum requirements for sampling by an inspector set forth in Annex 5 shall be complied with for the lamps.
requirements.test_case: Perform an Annex 5 random sampling of four lamps and evaluate deviations against 20/30 per cent limits.
requirements.why: Production lamps must pass the inspector sampling procedure.

requirements.text: No measured photometric value of production lamps shall deviate unfavourably by more than 20 per cent from the values prescribed in this Regulation.
requirements.test_case: Measure luminous intensity of random production samples at the prescribed points and verify deviation is at most 20 per cent.
requirements.why: Photometric CoP tolerance for rear position, stop and reversing lamps.

requirements.text: For the minimum values required throughout the fields specified in Annexes 2 and 3, the measured values shall correspond to Table 12: required minimum 7∙10^-1 cd → 5∙10^-1 cd (20 per cent) / 3∙10^-1 cd (30 per cent); 6∙10^-1 cd → 4∙10^-1 cd / 2∙10^-1 cd; 3∙10^-1 cd → 2∙10^-1 cd / 1∙10^-1 cd; 7∙10^-2 cd → 5∙10^-2 cd / 3∙10^-2 cd; 5∙10^-2 cd → 3∙10^-2 cd / 2∙10^-2 cd.
requirements.test_case: Measure the minimum-value points within the visibility fields and compare against the Table 12 equivalent values.
requirements.why: Table 12 defines CoP thresholds for low minimum values in the lamp's visibility fields.

requirements.text: Where doubt exists in respect of compliance of non-replaceable filament light sources with lifetime requirements (and colour endurance for colour-coated filament light sources), conformity shall be checked as specified in paragraph 4.11 of IEC 60809, Edition 4.
requirements.test_case: Confirm the light sources are LED (not filament); if any non-replaceable filament source is used, perform the IEC 60809 Ed.4 §4.11 lifetime check.
requirements.why: Borderline: applies only if non-replaceable filament sources are present; profile indicates LED modules, so confirm.

requirements.text: The production lamps shall conform from a mechanical and geometric standpoint, with differences not exceeding inevitable manufacturing deviations within the requirements of this Regulation.
requirements.test_case: Dimensional inspection of production lamps against approved drawings.
requirements.why: Mechanical/geometric CoP criterion for the lamp.

requirements.text: The chromaticity coordinates of the light emitted by production lamps shall be complied with when tested under the conditions of paragraph 4.9 of this Regulation.
requirements.test_case: Measure chromaticity of red (position/stop) and white (reversing) light of production samples per paragraph 4.9.
requirements.why: Colorimetric CoP requirement for red and white lamp functions.

requirements.text: The sampled lamp shall be subjected to photometric measurements for the minimum values at the points listed in Annex 3 and to the required chromaticity coordinates.
requirements.test_case: Measure the Annex 3 minimum-value points and chromaticity on sampled production lamps.
requirements.why: Defines the photometric/colorimetric CoP checks the lamp must pass.

requirements.text: With respect to photometric performance of any lamp chosen at random, no measured value shall deviate from the values prescribed in paragraph 6.1.3.
requirements.test_case: Test randomly selected lamps per paragraph 4.8 and compare against paragraph 6.1.3 limits.
requirements.why: Inspector sampling pass criterion for the lamp.

requirements.text: The chromaticity coordinates shall be complied with when tested under the conditions of paragraph 4.9 of this Regulation during inspector sampling.
requirements.test_case: Colorimetric measurement of randomly sampled lamps.
requirements.why: Colour CoP criterion in inspector sampling.

requirements.text: The deviation of any specimen of samples A and B (all four randomly selected lamps) shall be not more than 20 per cent.
requirements.test_case: Photometric test of four random lamps, each deviation not more than 20 per cent.
requirements.why: Pass criterion for first sampling of production lamps.

requirements.text: No specimen of repeated samples C or D shall deviate by more than 30 per cent, otherwise approval is withdrawn.
requirements.test_case: Photometric test of repeated samples, verify no deviation exceeds 30 per cent.
requirements.why: Absolute CoP limit leading to withdrawal of approval.

requirements.text: The angles of geometric visibility of Annex 2 apply as shown for lamps to be mounted on the right side of the vehicle; for lamps to be mounted on the left side of the vehicle, the inboard/outboard angles shall be applied mirrored.
requirements.test_case: Check that the goniometric visibility verification uses the correct inboard/outboard orientation for the side (left/right) on which the lamp is mounted.
requirements.why: The rear combination lamp is a side-mounted (left/right) rear lamp, so the side-specific orientation of the angles applies.

requirements.text: The rear position lamp (category R1, R2) shall have minimum horizontal angles of geometric visibility of 45° inboard / 80° outboard.
requirements.test_case: Measure the apparent surface visibility on a goniometer over horizontal angles 45° inboard to 80° outboard.
requirements.why: P-01 is a rear position lamp of category R1/R2 for an M1 vehicle (Table A2-1).

requirements.text: For a rear position lamp (R1, R2) mounted with the H-plane below 750 mm, reduced minimum horizontal angles of 20° inboard / 80° outboard may be used only below the H-plane.
requirements.test_case: For a mounting height below 750 mm, verify visibility below the H-plane over 20° inboard to 80° outboard.
requirements.why: Sets the horizontal visibility limit for the rear position function at low mounting height, typical of an M1 rear lamp.

requirements.text: The rear position lamp (R1, R2) shall have minimum vertical angles of geometric visibility of 15° above / 15° below the H-plane.
requirements.test_case: Verify the apparent surface is visible at 15° above and 15° below the H-plane.
requirements.why: Sets the vertical visibility limit for the rear position lamp (Table A2-1).

requirements.text: For a rear position lamp (R1, R2) to be installed with the H-plane at a mounting height of less than 750 mm, the minimum vertical angles shall be 15° above / 5° below the H-plane.
requirements.test_case: For a declared mounting height below 750 mm, verify visibility at 15° above and 5° below the H-plane.
requirements.why: Reduced vertical angles apply to M1 rear lamps mounted below 750 mm.

requirements.text: For an optional rear position lamp (R1, R2) to be installed with the H-plane at a mounting height of more than 2,100 mm, the minimum vertical angles shall be 5° above / 15° below the H-plane.
requirements.test_case: If the lamp is declared for a mounting height above 2,100 mm, verify visibility at 5° above and 15° below the H-plane.
requirements.why: Conditional vertical visibility limit for the rear position function.

requirements.text: The stop lamp (category S1, S2) shall have minimum horizontal angles of geometric visibility of 45° inboard / 45° outboard.
requirements.test_case: Measure the visibility of the stop lamp apparent surface on a goniometer over horizontal angles 45° inboard to 45° outboard.
requirements.why: P-02 is a stop lamp of category S1/S2 (Table A2-1).

requirements.text: For a stop lamp (S1, S2) mounted with the H-plane below 750 mm, reduced minimum horizontal angles of 20° inboard / 45° outboard may be used only below the H-plane.
requirements.test_case: For a mounting height below 750 mm, verify visibility below the H-plane over 20° inboard to 45° outboard.
requirements.why: Sets the horizontal visibility limit for the stop function at low mounting height.

requirements.text: The stop lamp (S1, S2) shall have minimum vertical angles of geometric visibility of 15° above / 15° below the H-plane.
requirements.test_case: Verify the stop lamp apparent surface is visible at 15° above and 15° below the H-plane.
requirements.why: Sets the vertical visibility limit for the stop lamp (Table A2-1).

requirements.text: For a stop lamp (S1, S2) to be installed with the H-plane at a mounting height of less than 750 mm, the minimum vertical angles shall be 15° above / 5° below the H-plane.
requirements.test_case: For a declared mounting height below 750 mm, verify visibility at 15° above and 5° below the H-plane.
requirements.why: Reduced vertical angles apply to a stop lamp mounted below 750 mm.

requirements.text: For an optional stop lamp (S1, S2) to be installed with the H-plane at a mounting height of more than 2,100 mm, the minimum vertical angles shall be 5° above / 15° below the H-plane.
requirements.test_case: If the lamp is declared for a mounting height above 2,100 mm, verify visibility at 5° above and 15° below the H-plane.
requirements.why: Conditional vertical visibility limit for the stop function.

requirements.text: The light intensity values in the various directions of measurement shall meet the minimum intensities given in Figures A3-I to A3-XV as a percentage of the minimum intensities required, mathematically rounded down to three significant digits, with H = 0° and V = 0° corresponding to the reference axis passing through the centre of reference.
requirements.test_case: Goniophotometer measurement of each lamp function at the grid directions, comparing results to the rounded-down percentage of the required minimum.
requirements.why: The rear position, stop and reversing lamps must meet the minimum intensity distribution defined by these figures.

requirements.text: Where the rear position lamp is intended to be installed at a mounting height (using the H plane specified by the manufacturer) equal to or less than 750 mm above the ground, the photometric intensity shall be verified only up to an angle of 5° downwards.
requirements.test_case: Check the declared mounting height; if ≤ 750 mm, verify rear position lamp photometry down to 5° below H only.
requirements.why: The product includes a rear position lamp, which is listed in (b).

requirements.text: Where the stop lamp of category S1, S2 or MS is intended to be installed at a mounting height (using the H plane specified by the manufacturer) equal to or less than 750 mm above the ground, the photometric intensity shall be verified only up to an angle of 5° downwards.
requirements.test_case: Check the declared mounting height; if ≤ 750 mm, verify stop lamp photometry down to 5° below H only.
requirements.why: The product includes a stop lamp (category S1/S2) listed in (e).

requirements.text: Within the field of light distribution schematically shown as a grid, the light intensity in each direction of a part of the field formed by the grid lines shall meet at least the lowest minimum value shown on the grid lines surrounding the questioned direction as a percentage.
requirements.test_case: Scan intermediate directions between grid points with a goniophotometer and confirm each value meets the lowest surrounding grid minimum.
requirements.why: Applies to the light distribution of the rear position, stop and reversing lamps.

requirements.text: In the case of reversing lamps, if visual examination of the lamp appears to reveal substantial local variations of intensity, no intensity measured between two of the directions of measurement shall be below 50 per cent of the lower minimum intensity of the two prescribed for these directions of measurement.
requirements.test_case: Visually inspect the reversing lamp beam; if local variations are seen, measure between adjacent grid directions and confirm ≥ 50 % of the lower prescribed minimum.
requirements.why: The product includes a reversing lamp.

requirements.text: The rear position lamp shall, for the various directions of measurement shown in Figure A3-I, emit at least the minimum luminous intensities given there as a percentage of the minimum intensity required for rear position lamps (see Table 4).
requirements.test_case: Goniophotometer measurement at each Figure A3-I grid point, compared with the Table 4 minimum multiplied by the grid percentage.
requirements.why: P-01 is a rear position lamp, and Figure A3-I is its prescribed standard light distribution.

requirements.text: The stop lamp of category S1, S2 or MS shall, for the various directions of measurement shown in Figure A3-I, emit at least the minimum luminous intensities given there as a percentage of the minimum intensity required in Table 7 (S1/S2: 6.0∙10^1 cd; MS: 4.0∙10^1 cd).
requirements.test_case: Goniophotometer measurement of the stop function at the Figure A3-I grid points against the percentage of the Table 7 minimum for the declared category.
requirements.why: P-02 is a rear combination stop lamp (S1/S2), and Figure A3-I applies to it.

requirements.text: The reversing lamp shall, at the measuring points given in Figure A3-V (expressed in degrees of angle from the axis of reference), emit luminous intensities not lower than the minimum values in cd shown in Figure A3-V.
requirements.test_case: Goniophotometer measurement of the reversing function at each Figure A3-V point, compared with the cd minimum shown.
requirements.why: P-03 is a reversing lamp, and Figure A3-V defines its minimum intensity distribution.

requirements.text: For the reversing lamp, the direction H = 0° and V = 0° shall correspond to the axis of reference, which on the vehicle shall be horizontal, parallel to the median longitudinal plane of the vehicle, oriented in the required direction of visibility, and passing through the centre of reference.
requirements.test_case: Check the declared reference axis and centre of reference in the drawings and the photometric set-up alignment.
requirements.why: This defines the reference geometry the reversing lamp's photometric conformity is verified against.

requirements.text: The lamps (rear position, stop and reversing lamp) shall conform to the approved type from a mechanical and geometric standpoint, with differences not exceeding inevitable manufacturing deviations within the requirements of this Regulation.
requirements.test_case: Dimensionally inspect production samples against the approved type drawings and check that deviations stay within manufacturing tolerances.
requirements.why: CoP mechanical/geometric conformity applies to every mass-produced lamp approved under R148.

requirements.text: Mass-produced lamps shall meet the photometric performance requirements when any lamp chosen at random is tested according to paragraph 4.8. of this Regulation.
requirements.test_case: Goniophotometer measurement of randomly selected production lamps per para 4.8 and comparison with the Annex 3 minimum and maximum values.
requirements.why: Photometric CoP criterion for the rear position, stop and reversing functions of the product.

requirements.text: Mass-produced lamps shall comply with the chromaticity coordinates (red for the rear position and stop lamps, white for the reversing lamp) when tested under the conditions of paragraph 4.9. of this Regulation.
requirements.test_case: Spectroradiometric measurement of production samples within the Annex 3 grid field, with the LED light sources fitted in the lamp.
requirements.why: Colorimetric CoP requirement for the light emitted by the lamp functions.

requirements.text: Conformity of production tests of the lamp shall cover both the photometric and the colorimetric characteristics.
requirements.test_case: Review the CoP test plan and records to confirm that photometric and colorimetric tests are performed for each lamp function.
requirements.why: Defines the characteristics of the product subject to CoP verification.

requirements.text: Conformity tests of the lamp shall generally be carried out in accordance with the methods set out in this Regulation.
requirements.test_case: Audit the CoP test procedures against the R148 para 4.8/4.9 methods.
requirements.why: Constrains the test conditions under which the product's conformity is verified.

requirements.text: The sampled lamp shall meet the minimum photometric values at the measuring points listed in Annex 3 for each function (rear position lamp, stop lamp, reversing lamp).
requirements.test_case: Measure luminous intensity at each Annex 3 grid point for each function and verify that the minimum values are met.
requirements.why: Specifies the photometric values the production lamp must achieve at CoP.

requirements.text: The sampled lamp shall meet the required chromaticity coordinates for each function.
requirements.test_case: Measure the chromaticity coordinates of each function on sampled lamps and check them against the colour boundaries.
requirements.why: Specifies the colorimetric values the production lamp must achieve at CoP.

requirements.text: Production lamps shall meet acceptability criteria such that, with a confidence level of 95 per cent, the minimum probability of passing a spot check in accordance with Annex 5 is 0.95.
requirements.test_case: Statistically analyse the CoP photometric and colorimetric results to show a ≥0.95 pass probability at 95 % confidence.
requirements.why: Quantitative statistical conformity limit that the production of the lamp must satisfy.

requirements.text: The mass-produced lamps (rear position, stop and reversing lamp functions) shall conform from a mechanical and a geometric standpoint to the requirements of this Regulation, with differences not exceeding inevitable manufacturing deviations.
requirements.test_case: Measure dimensions and inspect construction of production samples against the approved drawings and check that deviations are within normal manufacturing tolerances.
requirements.why: Conformity-of-production geometric/mechanical criterion applies to every approved lamp of this type.

requirements.text: When the photometric performances set forth in paragraph 4.8. are tested on any lamp chosen at random from mass production, no measured value shall deviate from the values prescribed in paragraph 6.1.3. (no unfavourable deviation of more than 20 per cent, with minimum values per Table 12).
requirements.test_case: Perform goniophotometric measurement of randomly selected production lamps and compare each point with the prescribed values within the 20 per cent CoP tolerance.
requirements.why: Photometric CoP pass criterion for the position, stop and reversing functions of the lamp.

requirements.text: In the case of a lamp equipped with a replaceable light source, if the photometric results do not meet the requirements, the lamp shall meet them when the tests are repeated using another standard light source.
requirements.test_case: If replaceable LED light sources are used and a test fails, repeat the photometric test with another standard light source and verify compliance.
requirements.why: Applies if the LED modules turn out to be replaceable light sources (replaceability to be confirmed).

requirements.text: The chromaticity coordinates of the light emitted by mass-produced lamps shall be complied with when tested under the conditions of paragraph 4.9. of this Regulation.
requirements.test_case: Measure chromaticity of red (position, stop) and white (reversing) light of production samples with the non-replaceable light sources fitted and compare with the colour limits.
requirements.why: Colorimetric CoP criterion for the red and white light emitted by the lamp.

requirements.text: For the first sampling of four lamps (samples A and B), the deviation of any specimen shall not be more than 20 per cent for the conformity of mass-produced lamps not to be contested.
requirements.test_case: Measure photometry of four randomly selected lamps and verify that no specimen deviates by more than 20 per cent.
requirements.why: Sets the 20 per cent CoP deviation limit the production lamps must meet.

requirements.text: The conformity of mass-produced lamps shall be contested if the deviation of at least one specimen of samples A or B is more than 20 per cent, and production shall be brought in line with the requirements before a repeated sampling within two months.
requirements.test_case: Evaluate first-sampling results; any specimen exceeding 20 per cent deviation triggers non-conformity and repeated sampling.
requirements.why: Defines the failure criterion for production lamps in the first CoP sampling.

requirements.text: For the first repeated sampling of four lamps from stock manufactured after alignment (samples C and D), the deviation of any specimen shall not be more than 20 per cent for the conformity of mass-produced lamps not to be contested.
requirements.test_case: Measure photometry of four randomly selected lamps produced after alignment and verify each deviates by no more than 20 per cent.
requirements.why: CoP deviation limit applying to the product after production alignment.

requirements.text: In the first repeated sampling, where at least one specimen of samples C or D deviates by more than 20 per cent, the deviation of all specimens of these samples shall not be more than 30 per cent, otherwise the approval is withdrawn; production shall be aligned again before a second repeated sampling.
requirements.test_case: Verify that all four specimens of samples C and D deviate by no more than 30 per cent (Table 12 30 per cent values).
requirements.why: Sets the 30 per cent absolute CoP limit for production lamps in the repeated sampling.

requirements.text: No specimen of samples C or D shall deviate by more than 30 per cent; if one does, the approval shall be withdrawn.
requirements.test_case: Check measured photometric values of samples C and D against the 30 per cent equivalent values in Table 12.
requirements.why: Exceeding 30 per cent deviation leads to withdrawal of the lamp approval.

requirements.text: For the second repeated sampling of four lamps from stock manufactured after alignment (samples E and F), the deviation of any specimen shall not be more than 20 per cent for the conformity of mass-produced lamps not to be contested.
requirements.test_case: Measure photometry of four randomly selected lamps and verify each deviates by no more than 20 per cent.
requirements.why: Final CoP deviation limit the production lamps must meet.

requirements.text: No specimen of samples E or F shall deviate by more than 20 per cent; if at least one does, the approval shall be withdrawn.
requirements.test_case: Evaluate second repeated sampling results against the 20 per cent limit.
requirements.why: Failure in the second repeated sampling results in withdrawal of the lamp approval.

requirements.text: The lamp shall withstand a one-hour test of continuous operation following a warm-up period of 20 minutes, at an ambient temperature of 23 °C ± 5 °C.
requirements.test_case: Operate the lamp for 20 min warm-up plus 1 h continuous in a 23 °C ± 5 °C chamber.
requirements.why: Heat resistance test conditions applicable to the rear lamp functions under R148.

requirements.text: For lamps equipped with non-replaceable light sources, the heat resistance test shall be made with the light sources present in the lamp.
requirements.test_case: Perform the heat test with the lamp's own non-replaceable LED modules installed and powered.
requirements.why: The product uses presumed non-replaceable LED modules.

requirements.text: For lamps equipped with non-replaceable light sources, the heat resistance test conditions set in paragraph 5.4.5. or 5.9.5. of the Regulation shall be applied, the specified power being chosen from the rated voltage(s) of 6, 12 or 24 V at which it reaches the highest value.
requirements.test_case: Verify supply voltage/power settings used in the heat test against the specified test voltage conditions.
requirements.why: Defines the electrical test condition the LED lamp must withstand.

requirements.text: In the case of light sources operated by an electronic control gear to obtain variable luminous intensity, the heat resistance test shall be carried out under the conditions giving at minimum 90 per cent of the higher luminous intensity.
requirements.test_case: Set the control gear to at least 90 % of the higher intensity level during the heat test and verify by measurement.
requirements.why: Applies if the LED PCB electronics provide variable intensity (e.g. stop/position).

requirements.text: After the lamp has been stabilized at the ambient temperature following the heat resistance test, no distortion, deformation, cracking or colour modification shall be perceptible.
requirements.test_case: Visually inspect lens, housing and optics after cooling to ambient for distortion, deformation, cracks or colour change.
requirements.why: Pass/fail criterion for lens and housing of the rear lamp.

requirements.text: In case of doubt, the luminous intensity measured according to paragraph 5. after the heat resistance test shall reach at least 90 per cent of the values obtained before the heat resistance test on the same lamp.
requirements.test_case: Measure photometric values before and after the heat test and confirm post-test values are ≥ 90 % of pre-test values.
requirements.why: Photometric pass/fail criterion after heat test for the lamp.

requirements.text: For the reversing lamp (light source technology other than incandescent), the luminous intensities measured after 1 minute of operation shall comply with the minimum and maximum requirements.
requirements.test_case: Switch on the reversing lamp from cold, measure the intensity distribution (or HV ratio-scaled distribution) after 1 min and compare with min/max limits.
requirements.why: Product includes an LED reversing lamp approved under R148.

requirements.text: For the reversing lamp (light source technology other than incandescent), the luminous intensities measured after 10 minutes of operation shall comply with the minimum and maximum requirements.
requirements.test_case: Measure the reversing lamp intensity distribution after 10 min of operation (or scale via HV ratio) and verify min/max compliance.
requirements.why: Product includes an LED reversing lamp approved under R148.

requirements.text: For the rear position lamp (light source technology other than incandescent), the luminous intensities measured after 1 min of operation shall comply with the minimum and maximum requirements.
requirements.test_case: Measure rear position lamp intensities after 1 min of operation (or scale via HV ratio) and verify against min/max limits.
requirements.why: Product includes an LED rear position lamp.

requirements.text: For the rear position lamp (light source technology other than incandescent), the luminous intensities measured either after 30 minutes of operation or after photometric stability has occurred shall comply with the minimum and maximum requirements.
requirements.test_case: Measure rear position lamp intensity distribution after 30 min or at photometric stability and verify against min/max limits.
requirements.why: Product includes an LED rear position lamp.

requirements.text: For the stop lamp (light source technology other than incandescent), the luminous intensities measured after 1 min of operation shall comply with the minimum and maximum requirements.
requirements.test_case: Measure stop lamp intensities after 1 min of operation (or scale via HV ratio) and verify against min/max limits.
requirements.why: Product includes an LED stop lamp.

requirements.text: For the stop lamp (light source technology other than incandescent), the luminous intensities measured either after 30 minutes of operation or after photometric stability has occurred shall comply with the minimum and maximum requirements.
requirements.test_case: Measure stop lamp intensity distribution after 30 min or at photometric stability and verify against min/max limits.
requirements.why: Product includes an LED stop lamp.

requirements.text: For the rear position lamp, the luminous intensity distribution shall additionally comply at 4 seconds after switch ON, using HV as reference coordinate (Table A8-1).
requirements.test_case: Measure intensity at HV 4 s after switch-on and scale the distribution by the HV ratio; verify compliance.
requirements.why: Table A8-1 row 'Front and rear position' applies to the rear position lamp.

requirements.text: For the stop lamp, the luminous intensity distribution shall additionally comply at 0.2 seconds after switch ON, using HV as reference coordinate (Table A8-1).
requirements.test_case: Measure intensity at HV 0.2 s after switch-on and scale the distribution by the HV ratio; verify compliance.
requirements.why: Table A8-1 row 'Stop' applies to the stop lamp.

requirements.text: For the reversing lamp, the luminous intensity distribution shall additionally comply at 0.2 seconds after switch ON, using HV as reference coordinate (Table A8-1).
requirements.test_case: Measure intensity at HV 0.2 s after switch-on and scale the distribution by the HV ratio; verify compliance.
requirements.why: Table A8-1 row 'Reversing' applies to the reversing lamp.

requirements.text: Where a lamp (function) uses LED technology only, it is deemed to comply with the corresponding intensity requirements at all points in time if the values measured according to paragraph 1.2. are compliant.
requirements.test_case: Confirm all functions use LED only and that the paragraph 1.2 measurements are compliant.
requirements.why: All three functions use LED modules only.

requirements.text: Where a lamp (function) uses more than one light generating technology, the intensity requirements shall be tested following the strictest time requirements according to paragraphs 2.1.1. to 2.1.3. for the combination and checked for compliance.
requirements.test_case: Verify the light generating technologies used per function; if mixed, test at the strictest time points.
requirements.why: Applies if any function combines LED with another light generating technology.

requirements.text: In case of doubt (e.g. unexpected run-up behaviour), the minimum intensity requirements of the rear position, stop and reversing lamp functions shall be complied with at all points in time starting at the corresponding point in time listed in Table A8-1 and ending when photometric stability is reached.
requirements.test_case: Record intensity at HV continuously from switch-on (4 s / 0.2 s) until photometric stability and verify minimum values are met throughout.
requirements.why: Run-up behaviour of LED functions may be checked against minimum intensities at all points in time.

requirements.text: The retro-reflector (Class IA) belonging to an approved type shall comprise a space of sufficient size for the Unique Identifier as referred to in the 1958 Agreement and other markings as defined in paragraph 3.3.4.2., or the approval marking and other markings as defined in paragraph 3.3.4.2.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the drawing and sample to confirm that a marking area large enough for the approval mark/UI and the TOP and trade-name markings exists.
requirements.why: The product includes a Class IA retro-reflector approved under UN R150, which must provide marking space.

requirements.text: All markings on the retro-reflector shall be clearly legible and indelible.
requirements.test_case: Visually inspect the markings and perform a rub/durability test, then confirm they remain legible.
requirements.why: This applies to all markings on the R150-approved retro-reflector.

requirements.text: The size of the approval marking of the Class IA retro-reflector shall be based on a minimum value of "a" of 5 mm as defined in Table 1.
requirements.test_case: Measure the dimension "a" of the approval mark on the sample and check that it is ≥ 5 mm.
requirements.why: Table 1 sets the minimum mark size for symbol IA, which is the product's retro-reflector class.

requirements.text: The approval marking shall include the approval mark, i.e. a circle surrounding the letter "E" followed by the distinguishing number of the country which has granted approval.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the marking for the circled E and the country number.
requirements.why: This is a mandatory element of the approval marking on the retro-reflector.

requirements.text: The approval marking shall include the four to six-digit sequential number that forms part of the approval number prescribed in paragraph 3.2.3.2.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the marking for the presence of the 4–6 digit sequential number.
requirements.why: This is a mandatory element of the approval marking on the retro-reflector.

requirements.text: The sequential number shall be placed close to the approval mark.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the marking layout to confirm the sequential number sits adjacent to the circled E.
requirements.why: This is a positional constraint on the retro-reflector marking.

requirements.text: The approval marking shall include the symbol identifying the retro-reflective device prescribed in paragraph 3.2.5., i.e. "IA" for the Class IA retro-reflector.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the marking for the class symbol "IA".
requirements.why: This is a mandatory class symbol for the product's Class IA retro-reflector.

requirements.text: The approval marking shall include the number of this Regulation followed by the letter "R" and the two digits indicating the series of amendments in force at the time of issue of the approval (e.g. 150R01).
requirements.test_case: Inspect the marking for "150R" followed by the two-digit amendment series.
requirements.why: This is a mandatory element of the approval marking on the retro-reflector.

requirements.text: Where the approval marking is replaced by the Unique Identifier, the Unique Identifier mark on the retro-reflective device shall follow the format shown in Figure I.
requirements.test_case: If a UI is used, compare the marking with the Figure I format.
requirements.why: This applies if the product uses the UI option instead of the approval marking.

requirements.text: The retro-reflector shall bear the trade name or mark of the applicant.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the sample for the applicant's trade name or mark.
requirements.why: This is a mandatory marking for the R150 retro-reflective device.

requirements.text: The Class IA retro-reflector shall bear the word "TOP" inscribed horizontally on the highest part of the illuminating surface, if such an indication is necessary to determine without ambiguity the angle or angles of rotation prescribed by the manufacturer.
requirements.test_case: Check whether the optic is rotationally asymmetric; if it is, verify that a horizontal "TOP" marking appears at the highest part of the illuminating surface.
requirements.why: This orientation marking applies specifically to Class IA retro-reflectors.

requirements.text: The approval marking or the Unique Identifier and the markings in paragraph 3.3.4. shall be clearly legible on the retro-reflective device.
requirements.test_case: Visually inspect the assembled device to confirm all required markings are legible.
requirements.why: This marking location requirement applies to the retro-reflector.

requirements.text: Where a single approval mark is affixed to the grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps (rear lamp incorporating the retro-reflector), the marking shall be visible after their installation.
requirements.test_case: Install the lamp on a representative vehicle body and check that the single approval mark is visible.
requirements.why: The retro-reflector is integrated into a rear combination lamp, so the single-mark option conditions apply.

requirements.text: Where a single approval mark is affixed to the grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps, no part of those lamps that transmits light shall be removable without at the same time removing the approval mark with the four to six-digit sequential number or the Unique Identifier.
requirements.test_case: Review the design and attempt disassembly to confirm that no light-transmitting part can be removed without also removing the mark.
requirements.why: This applies to the combination rear lamp if a single approval mark is used.

requirements.text: The size of the components of a single approval mark on the grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps shall not be less than the minimum size required for the smallest of the individual marks by the pertinent UN Regulations under which approval has been granted.
requirements.test_case: Measure the components of the single approval mark and compare them with the minimum sizes required by R150 and the lamp regulations.
requirements.why: This size constraint applies to a single combined mark on the rear combination lamp.

requirements.text: The retro-reflector shall comply with the requirements of sections 5 'General specifications' and 6 'Individual specifications' and the referenced Annexes of UN Regulation No. 48 (series of amendments in force at the time of application) pertinent to the retro-reflector and to the vehicle category (M1) on which it is intended to be installed, where verification at device type approval is feasible.
requirements.test_case: Review the applicable UN R48 installation provisions for rear Class IA retro-reflectors on M1 and verify the feasible ones on the device.
requirements.why: Applies to all retro-reflective devices approved under R150, including the Class IA retro-reflector in the lamp.

requirements.text: The retro-reflective device shall be so constructed that it functions satisfactorily and will continue to do so in normal use.
requirements.test_case: Check retro-reflection performance before and after the R150 durability and environmental tests.
requirements.why: General construction requirement for all retro-reflective devices, including the integrated Class IA retro-reflector.

requirements.text: The retro-reflective device shall not have any defect in design or manufacture that is detrimental to its efficient operation or to its maintenance in good condition.
requirements.test_case: Visually inspect samples for design or manufacturing defects such as cracks, voids or poor bonding.
requirements.why: General construction requirement for the retro-reflector.

requirements.text: The components of the retro-reflective device or parts thereof shall not be capable of being easily dismantled.
requirements.test_case: Attempt to dismantle the retro-reflector components by hand without tools and verify this is not possible.
requirements.why: Applies to the retro-reflector components integrated in the rear lamp.

requirements.text: The outer surface of the retro-reflective device shall be easy to clean.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the outer lens surface over the retro-reflector and perform a cleaning check.
requirements.why: The outer surface (lens) of the retro-reflector forms part of the product.

requirements.text: The outer surface of the retro-reflective device shall not be rough, and any protuberances it may exhibit shall not prevent easy cleaning.
requirements.test_case: Perform a tactile and visual inspection of surface roughness and protuberances on the outer surface.
requirements.why: Constrains the outer surface design of the retro-reflector and lens.

requirements.text: There shall be no access to the inner surface of the retro-reflector when in normal use.
requirements.test_case: With the lamp mounted as in use, inspect that the prism (inner) surface cannot be reached.
requirements.why: Applies to retro-reflectors such as the Class IA unit in the lamp.

requirements.text: Where the retro-reflector consists of a combined retro-reflecting optical unit and filter, these shall be so designed that they cannot be separated under normal conditions of use.
requirements.test_case: Check that the optical unit and filter are bonded or welded and cannot be separated under normal-use handling.
requirements.why: Relevant because the retro-reflector is integrated behind the red-tinted lens.

requirements.text: The retro-reflecting optical unit and filter shall not be coloured by means of paint or varnish.
requirements.test_case: Review the material specification and inspect that the red colour comes from mass-tinted PMMA, not a coating.
requirements.why: Applies to the colouring of the red Class IA retro-reflector.

requirements.text: When illuminated by CIE Standard Illuminant A with an angle of divergence of 1/3° and an illumination angle of β1 = β2 = 0° (or, if this produces a colourless surface reflection, the angle specified in Annex 4, Part 1, paragraph 1.1), the trichromatic coordinates of the reflected luminous intensity of the red retro-reflector shall be within the limits for the night-time red colour of retro-reflected light defined in UN Regulation No. 48.
requirements.test_case: Measure the chromaticity of retro-reflected light under Illuminant A at 1/3° divergence and compare it with the R48 red limits.
requirements.why: Night-time colour requirement for red retro-reflective devices such as the Class IA rear retro-reflector.

requirements.text: The night-time colour specifications shall apply to the red retro-reflective device (Class IA), as these specifications apply only to white, red or amber retro-reflective devices.
requirements.test_case: Confirm the retro-reflector is red and is therefore subject to the night-time colorimetric test of 4.2.1.2.
requirements.why: The product's Class IA retro-reflector is red, so it falls within the scope of the night-time colour specifications.

requirements.text: For testing the colour of the retro-reflective device, the device shall be illuminated by CIE Standard Illuminant A, with an angle of divergence of 1/3° and an illumination angle of β1 = β2 = 0°. If this produces a colourless surface reflection, the angle specified in Annex 4, Part 1, paragraph 1.1 (β1 = -5°, β2 = 0°) shall be used.
requirements.test_case: Illuminate the retro-reflector with CIE Illuminant A at 1/3° divergence and β1 = β2 = 0°, or at β1 = -5°, β2 = 0° if a mirror effect occurs, then measure the chromaticity of the reflected light.
requirements.why: These test conditions determine how the colour compliance of the product's red retro-reflector is verified.

requirements.text: The trichromatic coordinates of the reflected luminous intensity of the red retro-reflective device shall be within the limits for the night-time colour (red) of retro-reflected light as defined in UN Regulation No. 48.
requirements.test_case: Measure the x,y chromaticity of the retro-reflected light and check that it falls inside the R48 red night-time colour boundaries.
requirements.why: This is a colorimetric pass/fail limit for the product's red Class IA retro-reflector.

requirements.text: Every retro-reflector of Class IA, when tested according to paragraph 5.1.7., shall meet the dimensions and shape requirements set forth in Annex 5.
requirements.test_case: Visually inspect the retro-reflector's shape and dimensions against Annex 5 on all samples.
requirements.why: The rear lamp incorporates a Class IA retro-reflector (P-05).

requirements.text: Every retro-reflector of Class IA, when tested according to paragraph 5.1.7., shall meet the photometric and colorimetric requirements as specified in paragraphs 5.1.4. to 5.1.5.
requirements.test_case: Measure RI and night-time colour per Annex 4 Part 1 and paragraph 4.2.1.
requirements.why: Class IA retro-reflector photometry and colour apply to P-05.

requirements.text: Every retro-reflector of Class IA, when tested according to paragraph 5.1.7., shall meet the physical and mechanical requirements set forth in paragraph 5.1.7., depending on the nature of the materials and construction of the retro-reflective device.
requirements.test_case: Run the Table 4 test sequence (heat, water, fuels, oils, corrosion, rear face, stability, weathering) and check the results.
requirements.why: The physical tests apply to the moulded PMMA Class IA retro-reflector.

requirements.text: The retro-reflector samples shall be subjected to the heat resistance test described in Part 1 of Annex 6. At least one hour after this test, they shall meet the colorimetric characteristics of paragraph 5.1.5. and the RI of paragraph 5.1.4. for an angle of divergence of 20' and an illumination angle β1 = β2 = 0°, or if necessary in the position defined in Part 1 of Annex 4, paragraphs 1.1. and 1.2.
requirements.test_case: Expose to 65 °C for 48 h, rest for 1 h, then measure colour and RI at 20', β1 = β2 = 0°.
requirements.why: This is the heat-resistance gate the Class IA retro-reflector must pass.

requirements.text: The two retro-reflectors giving the minimum and maximum RI values after the heat test shall be fully tested as shown in paragraph 5.1.4.
requirements.test_case: Perform complete photometry on the minimum and maximum RI samples.
requirements.why: Full photometric compliance is required for the extreme samples of the product.

requirements.text: First group: the retro-reflector samples shall pass the water penetration test (Part 2 of Annex 6) and then the tests for resistance to fuels and lubricants (Parts 1 and 2 of Annex 7).
requirements.test_case: Run the water immersion test, then the fuel and oil wipe tests, and inspect the samples.
requirements.why: Environmental resistance applies to the lamp-integrated retro-reflector.

requirements.text: Second group: the retro-reflector samples shall, if necessary, pass the corrosion test in Part 4 of Annex 6 and then the abrasive-strength test of the rear face of the retro-reflective device in Part 5 of Annex 6.
requirements.test_case: Run the salt-mist test, then the rear-face brushing and fuel test, and inspect the samples.
requirements.why: Corrosion and rear-face resistance apply to the Class IA device.

requirements.text: Third group: the retro-reflector samples shall pass the test for stability in time of the optical properties of the retro-reflective device in Part 3 of Annex 4.
requirements.test_case: Perform the stability-in-time evaluation and re-measure colour and RI.
requirements.why: Optical stability applies to the Class IA retro-reflector.

requirements.text: Fourth group: the retro-reflector samples shall pass the resistance to weathering test (Part 6 of Annex 6).
requirements.test_case: Perform 500 h of accelerated weathering per EN ISO 4892-2, then measure colour and RI.
requirements.why: Weathering resistance applies to the PMMA retro-reflector.

requirements.text: After undergoing the tests referred to in paragraph 5.1.3.1., the retro-reflectors in each group shall have a colour which satisfies the conditions laid down in paragraph 5.1.5.
requirements.test_case: Check the night-time colour of each group after its test sequence.
requirements.why: This is the post-test colour criterion for the product's retro-reflector.

requirements.text: After undergoing the tests referred to in paragraph 5.1.3.1., the retro-reflectors in each group shall have an RI which satisfies paragraph 5.1.4. This shall be verified for an angle of divergence of 20' and an illumination angle of β1 = β2 = 0°, or if necessary in all positions specified in Part 1 of Annex 4, paragraphs 1.1. and 1.2.
requirements.test_case: Measure RI at 20', β1 = β2 = 0° on each group after testing and compare with Table 3.
requirements.why: This is the post-test photometric criterion for the retro-reflector.
