requirements.text: Where more than one axis of reference, or a range of axes, is specified by the manufacturer, the retro-reflector shall meet the photometric requirements for each axis of reference or for the extreme axes of the specified range.
requirements.test_case: Repeat the photometric measurements for each declared axis of reference or for the extreme axes of the range.
requirements.why: The photometric compliance of the product depends on its declared axes.

requirements.text: For photometric measurements of the Class IA retro-reflector, only the illuminating surface defined by the planes contiguous to the outermost parts of the optical system, and contained within a circle of 200 mm diameter, shall be considered.
requirements.test_case: Mask the device to the declared perimeter within a 200 mm diameter circle before measuring.
requirements.why: This constrains the retro-reflector's effective illuminating surface.

requirements.text: The illuminating surface of the retro-reflector considered for photometric measurements shall be limited to 100 cm2, though the surfaces of the retro-reflecting optical units need not attain this area.
requirements.test_case: Measure the illuminating-surface area and confirm the masked area is ≤ 100 cm2.
requirements.why: This is an area limit on the Class IA illuminating surface.

requirements.text: When measured as described in paragraph 3 of Part 1 of Annex 4, the RI of the red Class IA retro-reflector at an angle of divergence of 20' shall be at least 3.00∙10^2 mcd/lx at β1 = 0°, β2 = 0°; at least 2.00∙10^2 mcd/lx at β1 = ±10°, β2 = 0°; and at least 1.00∙10^2 mcd/lx at β1 = ±5°, β2 = ±20°.
requirements.test_case: Measure RI with a goniophotometer at 20' divergence at the specified illumination angles.
requirements.why: These Table 3 minima apply to the red Class IA retro-reflector.

requirements.text: When measured as described in paragraph 3 of Part 1 of Annex 4, the RI of the red Class IA retro-reflector at an angle of divergence of 1°30' shall be at least 5∙10^0 mcd/lx at β1 = 0°, β2 = 0°; at least 2.8∙10^0 mcd/lx at β1 = ±10°, β2 = 0°; and at least 2.5∙10^0 mcd/lx at β1 = ±5°, β2 = ±20°.
requirements.test_case: Measure RI with a goniophotometer at 1°30' divergence at the specified illumination angles.
requirements.why: These Table 3 minima apply to the red Class IA retro-reflector.

requirements.text: The retro-reflector shall not have RI values lower than those shown in the last two columns of Table 3 within the solid angle having the centre of reference as its apex and bounded by the planes intersecting along the lines (β1 = ±10°, β2 = 0°) and (β1 = ±5°, β2 = ±20°).
requirements.test_case: Scan RI inside the bounded solid angle and confirm no value falls below the limits.
requirements.why: This is a photometric continuity requirement for the Class IA device.

requirements.text: Where the Class IA retro-reflector is intended to be installed with its H plane at a mounting height less than 750 mm above the ground, the RI values shall be verified only up to an angle of 5° downwards.
requirements.test_case: For a declared mounting height below 750 mm, limit the downward photometric verification to 5°.
requirements.why: This defines the photometric field for a rear lamp mounted low on an M1 vehicle.

requirements.text: The night-time colour of the retro-reflector shall be tested according to the method described in paragraph 4.2.1.
requirements.test_case: Perform the night-time colour measurement per paragraph 4.2.1.
requirements.why: This is the colour verification method for the retro-reflector.

requirements.text: The trichromatic coordinates of the luminous flux reflected by the red retro-reflector shall be within the limits for the night-time colour red as specified in UN Regulation No. 48.
requirements.test_case: Measure the x,y chromaticity of the reflected light and compare with the UN R48 red limits.
requirements.why: The Class IA retro-reflector of the rear lamp is red.

requirements.text: The retro-reflector shall be subjected to the heat test of 48 h at 65 °C ± 2 °C followed by visual inspection for distortion, as per Table 4 for Class IA.
requirements.test_case: Expose to 65 °C ± 2 °C for 48 h and inspect visually for distortion.
requirements.why: This is the Table 4 test sequence applicable to the Class IA retro-reflector.

requirements.text: The retro-reflector shall be subjected to the water test of 10 min in normal position and 10 min in inverted position followed by visual inspection, then to colorimetry and photometry limited to 20' and β1 = β2 = 0°, as per Table 4.
requirements.test_case: Immerse the device in the normal and inverted positions, inspect it, then measure colour and RI.
requirements.why: This is the Table 4 test sequence for Class IA.

requirements.text: The retro-reflector shall be subjected to the motor fuels test (5 min) and the oils test (5 min) with visual inspection, followed by colorimetry and photometry limited to 20' and β1 = β2 = 0°, as per Table 4.
requirements.test_case: Wipe the device with the n-heptane/toluol mixture and with detergent oil, inspect it, then measure colour and RI.
requirements.why: This is the Table 4 test sequence for Class IA.

requirements.text: The retro-reflector shall be subjected to the corrosion test (24 hours, 2 hours interval, 24 hours) and the rear face test (1 min) with visual inspection, followed by colorimetry and photometry limited to 20' and β1 = β2 = 0°, as per Table 4.
requirements.test_case: Perform the salt-mist and rear-face tests, inspect the device, then measure colour and RI.
requirements.why: This is the Table 4 test sequence for Class IA.

requirements.text: The shape of the illuminating surfaces of the Class IA retro-reflector shall not be easily confused with the triangular shape prescribed for Class IIIA/IIIB retro-reflectors, from an observation distance of 10 metres.
requirements.test_case: Visually inspect the retro-reflector from 10 m.
requirements.why: This is the shape requirement referenced by paragraph 5.1.1(a) for Class IA.

requirements.text: After the heat test, no cracking or appreciable distortion of the retro-reflective device and, in particular, of its optical component shall be visible.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the device visually after 48 h at 65 °C.
requirements.why: This is the pass criterion of the heat test required by paragraph 5.1.3.1.

requirements.text: After the water immersion test, no water shall penetrate to the reflecting surface of the retro-reflecting optical unit.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the device visually after immersion and measure RI in case of doubt.
requirements.why: This is the pass criterion of the water penetration test for a lamp-integrated retro-reflector.

requirements.text: Immediately after completion of the corrosion test, the retro-reflective device (or the lamp, if combined) shall not show signs of excessive corrosion liable to impair the efficiency of the device.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the device after 50 h of salt mist.
requirements.why: This is the pass criterion of the corrosion test required by paragraph 5.1.3.1.

requirements.text: After being wiped with the n-heptane/toluol test mixture, the outer surface of the retro-reflective device shall not show any apparent surface changes after about five minutes, except that slight surface cracks will not be objected to.
requirements.test_case: Wipe the illuminating surface with the test mixture and inspect it after 5 min.
requirements.why: This is the pass criterion of the fuel resistance test for the outer surface of the retro-reflector.

requirements.text: From a mechanical and geometric standpoint, mass-produced retro-reflective devices shall not differ from the approved type by more than inevitable manufacturing deviations within the requirements of this Regulation.
requirements.test_case: Dimensional and visual inspection of production samples against approved type drawings.
requirements.why: The Class IA retro-reflector P-05 is subject to R150 conformity of production.

requirements.text: When the photometric performance of any retro-reflective device chosen at random from mass production is tested, no measured value shall deviate unfavourably by more than 20 per cent from the minimum values prescribed in this Regulation.
requirements.test_case: Measure CIL of randomly sampled production retro-reflectors and compare with R150 minimum values minus 20 per cent.
requirements.why: The CoP photometric tolerance applies to the integrated Class IA retro-reflector.

requirements.text: The chromaticity coordinates of mass-produced retro-reflective devices shall comply with the requirements of this Regulation.
requirements.test_case: Colorimetric measurement of production samples against the red chromaticity limits.
requirements.why: The red Class IA retro-reflector shall maintain its colour in series production.

requirements.text: For each type of retro-reflective device, conformity tests shall be carried out at appropriate intervals in accordance with the provisions of this Regulation, and further samples shall be taken and tested if any sampling shows non-conformity.
requirements.test_case: Audit the CoP test plan and records for test intervals and re-sampling after failures.
requirements.why: Defines the minimum CoP verification for the retro-reflector type.

requirements.text: Conformity tests of the retro-reflective device shall cover the photometric and colorimetric characteristics and the resistance to penetration of water.
requirements.test_case: Verify that the CoP plan includes photometric, colorimetric and water penetration tests, and run them on production samples.
requirements.why: Production retro-reflectors shall pass these characteristics in CoP testing.

requirements.text: Conformity tests on the retro-reflective device shall generally be carried out in accordance with the methods set out in this Regulation.
requirements.test_case: Check that the CoP test procedures reference the R150 test methods.
requirements.why: Constrains the test conditions under which the product's conformity is verified.

requirements.text: Samples of retro-reflective devices for conformity testing shall be selected at random from the production of a uniform batch.
requirements.test_case: Review sampling records for random selection from a uniform batch.
requirements.why: Sets the sampling basis for CoP of the retro-reflector.

requirements.text: The sampled retro-reflective device shall be subjected to photometric measurements at the points, and to the chromaticity coordinates, provided for in this Regulation.
requirements.test_case: Measure CIL at all prescribed observation/entrance angle points and measure chromaticity on production samples.
requirements.why: Defines the measured characteristics the production retro-reflector shall meet.

requirements.text: The acceptability criteria for the retro-reflective devices shall be such that, with a confidence level of 95 per cent, the minimum probability of passing a spot check in accordance with Annex 3 (first sampling) would be 0.95.
requirements.test_case: Statistical analysis of CoP results showing at least 0.95 pass probability at 95 per cent confidence.
requirements.why: The production capability of the retro-reflector shall meet this statistical CoP criterion.

requirements.text: The mass-produced retro-reflector (Class IA) shall conform from a mechanical and a geometric standpoint to the requirements of this Regulation, with differences not exceeding inevitable manufacturing deviations.
requirements.test_case: Dimensional and visual inspection of randomly selected production samples against the approved type drawings.
requirements.why: CoP mechanical/geometric conformity applies to the approved Class IA retro-reflector incorporated in the rear lamp.

requirements.text: When testing photometric performance of any retro-reflective device chosen at random from production, no measured value shall deviate unfavourably by more than 20 per cent from the minimum values prescribed in this Regulation.
requirements.test_case: Measure CIL of randomly selected production retro-reflectors and compare with 80 per cent of the prescribed minimum values.
requirements.why: CoP photometric tolerance applicable to the Class IA retro-reflector.

requirements.text: Retro-reflective devices with apparent defects shall be disregarded when assessing photometric conformity of production.
requirements.test_case: Visually inspect samples before photometric testing and exclude those with apparent defects.
requirements.why: Defines which production retro-reflectors count in the CoP photometric assessment.

requirements.text: The mass-produced retro-reflective device shall comply with the prescribed chromaticity coordinates (red for the Class IA rear retro-reflector).
requirements.test_case: Colorimetric measurement of production samples against the red chromaticity limits.
requirements.why: CoP colorimetric requirement for the red Class IA retro-reflector.

requirements.text: In the first sampling (four randomly selected retro-reflective devices, samples A and B), the deviation of any specimen of samples A and B shall not be more than 20 per cent for conformity not to be contested.
requirements.test_case: Photometrically test four random devices (A and B) and verify no specimen deviates by more than 20 per cent.
requirements.why: CoP sampling acceptance criterion for the retro-reflector.

requirements.text: If the deviation of at least one specimen of samples A or B is more than 20 per cent, conformity of production of the retro-reflective devices shall be contested and production shall be brought in line with the requirements before a repeated sampling.
requirements.test_case: Check first-sampling results; any specimen exceeding 20 per cent deviation triggers alignment and repeated sampling.
requirements.why: Defines failure criterion of first CoP sampling for the retro-reflector.

requirements.text: In the first repeated sampling (four devices from stock manufactured after alignment, samples C and D), the deviation of any specimen of samples C and D shall not be more than 20 per cent for conformity not to be contested.
requirements.test_case: Photometrically test four random post-alignment devices (C and D) and verify no specimen deviates by more than 20 per cent.
requirements.why: CoP repeated-sampling acceptance criterion for the retro-reflector.

requirements.text: If one specimen of samples C or D deviates by more than 20 per cent but all specimens deviate by not more than 30 per cent, conformity shall be contested and production shall again be aligned before a second repeated sampling.
requirements.test_case: Evaluate C/D deviations between 20 and 30 per cent and confirm second repeated sampling is required.
requirements.why: CoP repeated-sampling criterion binding the retro-reflector production.

requirements.text: If one specimen of samples C and D deviates by more than 30 per cent, the approval of the retro-reflective device shall be withdrawn.
requirements.test_case: Check that no C/D specimen deviates by more than 30 per cent from the prescribed minimum values.
requirements.why: Sets the 30 per cent limit beyond which retro-reflector approval is lost.

requirements.text: In the second repeated sampling (four devices from stock manufactured after alignment, samples E and F), the deviation of any specimen of samples E and F shall not be more than 20 per cent for conformity not to be contested.
requirements.test_case: Photometrically test four random post-alignment devices (E and F) and verify no specimen deviates by more than 20 per cent.
requirements.why: CoP second repeated-sampling acceptance criterion for the retro-reflector.

requirements.text: If the deviation of at least one specimen of samples E or F is more than 20 per cent, the approval of the retro-reflective device shall be withdrawn.
requirements.test_case: Verify no E/F specimen exceeds 20 per cent deviation.
requirements.why: Final CoP failure criterion for the retro-reflector.

requirements.text: One of the retro-reflectors of sample A shall pass the resistance to water penetration test according to paragraph 1. of Part 2 of Annex 6 (no water penetrating to the reflecting surface of the retro-reflecting optical unit).
requirements.test_case: Immerse the retro-reflector (as part of the lamp, stripped of removable parts) 10 min in 50 °C water both ways up, then in 25 °C water, and inspect for water / re-measure CIL.
requirements.why: CoP water penetration check applies to Class IA retro-reflectors, including those part of a lamp.

requirements.text: If the water penetration test on sample A is not complied with, both retro-reflective devices of sample B shall be subjected to the same procedure and both shall pass the test.
requirements.test_case: On failure of sample A, test both sample B devices to Annex 6 Part 2 paragraph 1 and verify both pass.
requirements.why: Second-chance CoP water penetration criterion for the retro-reflector.

requirements.text: When the RI of the retro-reflective device is measured for an angle β of β1 = β2 = 0°, it shall be ascertained whether any mirror effect is produced by slightly turning the device; if there is any such effect, a reading shall be taken with an angle β of β1 = -5°, β2 = 0°.
requirements.test_case: Turn the device slightly about β1 = β2 = 0° on the goniometer; if a mirror effect appears, measure RI at β1 = -5°, β2 = 0°.
requirements.why: Defines the angle at which the Class IA retro-reflector's RI is judged when a mirror effect is present.

requirements.text: For retro-reflective devices not marked "TOP", with an illumination angle β of β1 = β2 = 0° (or the angle specified in paragraph 5) and an angle of divergence of 20', the device rotated about its axis of reference to the position of minimum RI shall conform to the RI value specified in paragraph 5 of this Regulation.
requirements.test_case: Rotate the unmarked device about its reference axis at β = 0°, α = 20', find the minimum RI and compare it with the paragraph 5 value.
requirements.why: Pass/fail criterion for the RI of a retro-reflector without a TOP marking.

requirements.text: For retro-reflective devices not marked "TOP", when the RI is measured for the other angles of illumination and divergence, the device shall be placed in the position corresponding to the minimum-RI value of ε. If the specified values are not attained there, the device may be rotated about its axis of reference by ±5° from that position.
requirements.test_case: Measure RI at all specified β/α combinations with the device fixed at the minimum-RI ε, using up to ±5° rotation only if the values are not met.
requirements.why: Sets the orientation in which the retro-reflector must meet the remaining RI values.

requirements.text: For retro-reflective devices marked "TOP", with an illumination angle β of β1 = β2 = 0° (or the angle specified in paragraph 4) and an angle of divergence of 20', the device shall be rotated about its axis by ±5°, and the RI shall not fall below the prescribed value in any position assumed by the device during this rotation.
requirements.test_case: Rotate the TOP-marked device ±5° about its reference axis at β = 0°, α = 20' and check that RI stays at or above the minimum throughout.
requirements.why: Pass/fail criterion for the RI of a retro-reflector carrying a TOP marking.

requirements.text: If, for the direction β1 = β2 = 0° and for ε = 0°, the RI exceeds the specified value by 50 per cent or more, all measurements for all angles of illumination and divergence shall be made for ε = 0°.
requirements.test_case: Compare the RI at β = 0°, ε = 0° with the specified value; if it is ≥150 %, measure all angles at ε = 0°.
requirements.why: Sets the rotation position in which the retro-reflector's RI compliance is assessed.

requirements.text: The CIE angular system shall be used for specifying and measuring the retro-reflective device.
requirements.test_case: Check that the test report states all angles (β1, β2, α, ε) in the CIE co-ordinate system.
requirements.why: Defines the angular reference system for the retro-reflector's photometric requirements.

requirements.text: For testing the retro-reflection, the retro-reflective device shall be illuminated with a CIE Standard Illuminant A (ISO 11664-2:2007(E)/CIE S 014-2/E:2006) and measured as described in Part 1 of Annex 4.
requirements.test_case: Verify that the source is calibrated to CIE Standard Illuminant A during the RI measurement.
requirements.why: Defines the illumination condition under which the retro-reflector's RI must comply.

requirements.text: In the measuring geometry for the retro-reflective device, the following limits shall apply: angular diameter of the source δ ≤ 10', angular diameter of the measuring device γ ≤ 10', and angular diameter of the illuminated area η ≤ 80'.
requirements.test_case: Calculate δ, γ and η from the source, receiver and device dimensions and the test distance, and check them against the limits.
requirements.why: Limits the measurement geometry that governs the retro-reflector's RI values.

requirements.text: The measuring distance shall be chosen so that at least the limits for the angles δ, γ and η are respected, but shall not be lower than 10 m.
requirements.test_case: Measure the source-to-device distance and confirm it is ≥10 m and meets the angular limits.
requirements.why: Sets the test distance for the retro-reflector's photometric measurement.

requirements.text: The illuminance over the useful area of the retro-reflective device, measured perpendicular to the incident light, shall be sufficiently uniform, such that the variation in illuminance complies with max/min ≤ 1.05, checked with a measuring element whose sensitive area is not greater than one-tenth of the area examined.
requirements.test_case: Scan the useful area with a small sensor (≤1/10 of the area) and verify max/min illuminance ≤ 1.05.
requirements.why: Test condition that constrains the validity of the retro-reflector's RI result.

requirements.text: The photometer head used for measuring the retro-reflective device shall be corrected to the spectral luminous efficiency for the CIE standard photometric observer in photopic vision.
requirements.test_case: Check the V(λ) calibration certificate of the photometer head.
requirements.why: Measurement condition for determining the retro-reflector's RI.

requirements.text: The photometer head shall not show a perceptible change in local sensitivity within the area of its aperture; otherwise suitable provisions shall be added, e.g. a diffusing window at a certain distance in front of the sensitive surface.
requirements.test_case: Check the uniformity of the photometer head's sensitivity across its aperture, or confirm that a diffusing window is fitted.
requirements.why: Measurement condition for determining the retro-reflector's RI.

requirements.text: The residual stray light measured with the sample covered by an opaque matt black surface (or equivalent light trap) shall be subtracted from the value measured on the retro-reflective device.
requirements.test_case: Measure the reading with the sample covered and subtract it from the RI measurement.
requirements.why: Determines the corrected RI value against which the retro-reflector is judged.

requirements.text: The shape of the illuminating surfaces of the Class IA retro-reflective device shall not be easily confused with the triangular shape, as prescribed for retro-reflectors mentioned in paragraph 2.1., from an observation distance of 10 metres.
requirements.test_case: Visually inspect the retro-reflector illuminating surface from 10 m and confirm it cannot be easily confused with a triangle.
requirements.why: The product includes a Class IA retro-reflector (P-05), whose illuminating-surface shape is constrained by this paragraph.

requirements.text: The moulded plastics retro-reflective device of Class IA shall be kept for 48 consecutive hours in a dry atmosphere at a temperature of 65 °C ± 2 °C, after which the sample shall be allowed to cool for 1 hour at 23 °C ± 2 °C.
requirements.test_case: Condition the Class IA retro-reflector in a dry oven at 65 °C ± 2 °C for 48 h, then cool for 1 h at 23 °C ± 2 °C.
requirements.why: Heat-resistance test condition applicable to the product's moulded PMMA Class IA retro-reflector.

requirements.text: After the heat resistance test, no cracking or appreciable distortion of the retro-reflective device and, in particular, of its optical component must be visible.
requirements.test_case: Visually inspect the retro-reflector after heat conditioning for cracks or distortion, especially of the prism optical component.
requirements.why: Pass/fail criterion for the heat resistance test of the Class IA retro-reflector.

requirements.text: The retro-reflective device, whether part of a lamp or not, shall be stripped of all removable parts and immersed for 10 minutes in water at a temperature of 50 °C ± 5 °C, the highest point of the upper part of the illuminating surface being 20 mm below the surface of the water.
requirements.test_case: Strip removable parts and immerse the lamp/retro-reflector for 10 min in 50 °C ± 5 °C water with the top of the illuminating surface 20 mm below the water surface.
requirements.why: The lamp incorporates a Class IA retro-reflector, which must withstand the water penetration resistance test.

requirements.text: The immersion test shall be repeated after turning the retro-reflective device through 180°, so that the illuminating surface is at the bottom and the rear face is covered by about 20 mm of water.
requirements.test_case: Invert the sample 180° and repeat the 10 min 50 °C immersion with the rear face about 20 mm under water.
requirements.why: Test condition the Class IA retro-reflector of the rear lamp must withstand.

requirements.text: The retro-reflective device shall then be immediately immersed under the same conditions in water at a temperature of 25 °C ± 5 °C.
requirements.test_case: Immediately transfer the sample to 25 °C ± 5 °C water under the same immersion conditions.
requirements.why: Thermal-shock immersion condition applicable to the Class IA retro-reflector.

requirements.text: No water shall penetrate to the reflecting surface of the retro-reflecting optical unit after the immersion test.
requirements.test_case: Visually inspect the reflecting surface of the retro-reflector optical unit for water after immersion.
requirements.why: Pass criterion for water tightness of the Class IA retro-reflector in the lamp.

requirements.text: If visual inspection clearly reveals the presence of water, the retro-reflective device shall not be considered to have passed the test.
requirements.test_case: Record fail if any water is clearly visible at the reflecting surface.
requirements.why: Defines failure of the Class IA retro-reflector in the water penetration test.

requirements.text: If visual inspection does not reveal the presence of water or in case of doubt, the RI of the retro-reflector shall be measured by the method described in paragraph 5.1.3.2.2. (satisfying the conditions of paragraph 5.1.4. at a divergence angle of 20' and illumination angle β1 = β2 = 0°), the retro-reflective device being first lightly shaken to remove excess water from the outside.
requirements.test_case: After lightly shaking off excess water, measure RI at 20' divergence and β1 = β2 = 0° and verify it meets the paragraph 5.1.4 minimum values.
requirements.why: Photometric post-test criterion for the Class IA retro-reflector where water ingress is not visually evident.

requirements.text: Where the manufacturer requests the alternative sealing test (for Class IB / IIIB retro-reflecting devices), the device shall be subjected to the moisture test and the dust test of Annex 6 Part 3.
requirements.test_case: Check the test report confirms both the moisture and dust tests were performed when the alternative route is chosen.
requirements.why: Applies only if the integrated retro-reflector is treated as Class IB and the alternative sealing test route is chosen.

requirements.text: During the moisture test, the precipitation rate of the water spray at the device shall be 2.5 (+1.6/-0) mm/min, measured with a vertical cylindrical collector 100 mm high with an inside diameter of at least 140 mm, centred on the vertical axis of the rotating platform.
requirements.test_case: Measure the collector fill rate before the test.
requirements.why: Sets the water-spray severity the lamp housing must withstand.

requirements.text: During the water spray test, all drain holes and other openings of the device shall remain open, and any drain wicks used shall be tested in the device.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the sample before the test to confirm vents and drain holes are unobstructed and wicks are fitted.
requirements.why: The lamp must pass with its production vents and drains in their open state.

requirements.text: During the water spray test, the device shall be rotated about its vertical axis at 4.0 ± 0.5 min-1.
requirements.test_case: Verify the platform speed with a tachometer.
requirements.why: Defines the test condition the sample must withstand.

requirements.text: If the retro-reflector is reciprocally incorporated or grouped with signalling or lighting functions, these functions (rear position, stop and reversing lamps) shall be operated at design voltage on a cycle of 5 min ON and 55 min OFF during the water spray test.
requirements.test_case: Record the lamp supply voltage and ON/OFF cycle timing during the spray test.
requirements.why: The retro-reflector is grouped with the rear position, stop and reversing lamps.

requirements.text: The water spray test shall last 12 hours (12 cycles of 5/55 min).
requirements.test_case: Check the test log duration.
requirements.why: Defines the exposure duration the lamp must withstand.

requirements.text: After spraying, the device shall be left to drain for 1 hour with rotation and spray turned OFF and the cabinet door closed.
requirements.test_case: Check the test log for a 1 h drain period with the door closed.
requirements.why: Defines the drainage condition before the pass/fail evaluation.

requirements.text: Upon completion of the drain period, no standing pool of water shall be formed inside the device, nor be capable of forming when the device is tapped or tilted.
requirements.test_case: Visually inspect the interior, then tap and tilt the device and check for pooled water.
requirements.why: This is the pass/fail sealing criterion for the lamp housing and lens.

requirements.text: After the moisture test, the exterior of the device shall be dried with a dry cotton cloth and the RI of the retro-reflector shall be measured according to Part 1 of Annex 4.
requirements.test_case: Measure RI after the test and compare it with the initial value and the specified limits.
requirements.why: Retro-reflector performance must be verified after moisture exposure.

requirements.text: During the dust exposure test, all drain holes and other openings of the device shall remain open, and any drain wicks used shall be tested in the device.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the sample before the dust test to confirm openings are open.
requirements.why: The lamp must resist dust with its vents in production configuration.

requirements.text: The device shall be exposed to fine cement test dust (ASTM C 150-84), agitated at 15 min intervals for periods of 2 to 15 s over 5 hours, with the device placed no closer than 150 mm from a chamber wall; a device longer than 600 mm shall be horizontally centred.
requirements.test_case: Check the dust chamber log and sample positioning.
requirements.why: Defines the dust exposure the lamp must withstand.

requirements.text: After the dust exposure test, the exterior of the device shall be cleaned and dried with a dry cotton cloth, and the RI shall be measured according to paragraph 5.1.3.2.2 (20' divergence, β1 = β2 = 0°) and shall satisfy paragraph 5.1.4.
requirements.test_case: Measure RI after the dust test and verify it meets the limits of 5.1.4.
requirements.why: This is the pass/fail criterion for dust penetration affecting retro-reflector output.

requirements.text: The retro-reflective device shall be so designed that it retains the prescribed photometric and colorimetric characteristics despite the humidity and corrosive influences to which it is normally exposed.
requirements.test_case: Perform the ISO 9227:2017 saline mist test, then re-measure photometry and colour against the prescribed limits.
requirements.why: The product includes a Class IA retro-reflector, which is subject to the corrosion resistance requirement.

requirements.text: The front surface of the retro-reflective device shall resist tarnishing and the protection of its rear face shall resist deterioration, particularly where an essential metal component seems liable to be attacked, as tested per ISO Standard 9227:2017.
requirements.test_case: After the salt spray test, visually inspect the front surface for tarnishing and the rear face protection for deterioration.
requirements.why: The retro-reflector, and the lamp with its metallised reflector, must resist corrosion of their front and rear surfaces.

requirements.text: The retro-reflective device, or the lamp if the device is combined with a light, shall withstand, stripped of all removable parts, the action of a saline mist for a period of 50 hours, comprising two exposure periods of 24 hours each separated by an interval of two hours during which the sample is allowed to dry.
requirements.test_case: Strip the lamp of removable parts and expose it to salt mist for 24 h + 2 h drying + 24 h.
requirements.why: The retro-reflector is combined with the rear lamp, so the whole lamp is the test sample.

requirements.text: For retro-reflective devices with essential metal components susceptible to corrosion, the saline mist shall be produced by atomizing, at a temperature of 35 °C ± 2 °C, a saline solution of 5 parts by weight of sodium chloride in 95 parts of distilled water containing not more than 0.02 per cent of impurities.
requirements.test_case: Verify that the salt spray chamber temperature is 35 ± 2 °C and that the solution is 5 % NaCl with ≤0.02 % impurities.
requirements.why: This test condition applies if the combined lamp/retro-reflector has essential metal parts, such as the aluminium-metallised reflector.

requirements.text: Immediately after completion of the corrosion test, the sample shall not show signs of excessive corrosion liable to impair the efficiency of the device.
requirements.test_case: Visually inspect the sample immediately after the salt spray exposure for corrosion that would impair its function.
requirements.why: This is the pass/fail criterion for the retro-reflector or combined lamp after the corrosion test.

requirements.text: After the corrosion test, the coefficient of retro-reflection RA of the retro-reflective areas, measured after a recovery period of 48 hours as specified in Part 2 of Annex 6, at an entrance angle of β2 = 5° and an observation angle of α = 20', and with the surface cleaned of salt deposits before measuring, shall be not less than the value in Table 9 or more than the value in Table 10 respectively.
requirements.test_case: After 48 h recovery and removal of salt deposits, measure RA at β2 = 5°, α = 20' and compare with the tabulated limits.
requirements.why: This is the photometric pass/fail criterion for the Class IA retro-reflector after corrosion exposure.

requirements.text: Where the Class IA retro-reflector is a mirror-backed moulded plastics reflector with an accessible rear face, the rear face shall be resistant to the test procedure of Annex 6 Part 5.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the retro-reflector construction for mirror backing and an accessible rear face; if present, run the Annex 6 Part 5 rear-face resistance test.
requirements.why: The product contains a Class IA moulded plastics (PMMA) retro-reflector, which is within the scope of this test.

requirements.text: For the rear-face resistance test, the reverse side of the Class IA retro-reflective device shall be brushed with a hard nylon brush.
requirements.test_case: Brush the reverse side of the sample with a hard nylon brush.
requirements.why: This test condition applies to the product's Class IA moulded plastics retro-reflector.

requirements.text: After brushing the rear face of the Class IA moulded plastics retro-reflective device, a cotton cloth soaked in the mixture defined in Annex 7 Part 1 (70 vol. per cent n-heptane and 30 vol. per cent toluol) shall be applied to the rear face for one minute. The cloth shall then be removed and the device left to dry.
requirements.test_case: Apply a cotton cloth soaked in the n-heptane/toluol mixture to the rear face for 1 min, remove it and let the device dry.
requirements.why: This fuel exposure condition is specified for Class IA moulded plastics reflectors.

requirements.text: As soon as evaporation is completed, the reverse side of the Class IA retro-reflective device shall be brushed with the same brush as before.
requirements.test_case: After drying, brush the reverse side again with the same hard nylon brush.
requirements.why: This is a step of the rear-face resistance test that the Class IA reflector must withstand.

requirements.text: After the whole surface of the mirror-backed rear face has been covered with Indian ink, the RI of the Class IA retro-reflective device shall be measured according to paragraph 5.1.3.2.2. It shall satisfy the conditions laid down in paragraph 5.1.4 at an angle of divergence of 20' and an illumination angle of β1 = β2 = 0°, or if necessary in all positions specified in Annex 4 Part 1.
requirements.test_case: Cover the rear face with Indian ink, measure the RI at 20' divergence and β1 = β2 = 0°, and compare it with the paragraph 5.1.4 minimum values.
requirements.why: This sets the photometric pass criterion after the rear-face resistance test for the product's Class IA retro-reflector.

requirements.text: The retro-reflective device shall be subjected to the fuel resistance test using a test mixture of 70 vol. per cent of n-heptane and 30 vol. per cent of toluol.
requirements.test_case: Prepare 70/30 vol.% n-heptane/toluol mixture and apply it to the retro-reflector sample.
requirements.why: The lamp incorporates a Class IA retro-reflector subject to the R150 fuel resistance test.

requirements.text: When the outer surface of the retro-reflective device, and in particular of the illuminating surface, is lightly wiped with a cotton cloth soaked in the test mixture, it shall not show any apparent surface changes on visual inspection after about five minutes, except that slight surface cracks will not be objected to.
requirements.test_case: Wipe the retro-reflector outer surface with a soaked cotton cloth, wait about 5 min, and visually inspect for surface changes other than slight cracks.
requirements.why: This is the pass/fail criterion for the fuel resistance of the retro-reflective device (P-05).

requirements.text: For the moulded plastics Class IA retro-reflector, the outer surface of the retro-reflective device and, in particular, the illuminating surface, shall withstand being lightly wiped with a cotton cloth soaked in a detergent lubricating oil and, after about 5 minutes, cleaned.
requirements.test_case: Wipe the outer and illuminating surfaces with a cotton cloth soaked in detergent lubricating oil, wait about 5 minutes, clean, then inspect.
requirements.why: P-05 is a moulded PMMA Class IA retro-reflector, so the lubricating-oil resistance test procedure applies to it.

requirements.text: After the lubricating oil test, the RI of the Class IA retro-reflector shall be measured according to paragraph 5.1.3.2.2. and shall satisfy the conditions laid down in paragraph 5.1.4., verified for an angle of divergence of 20' and an illumination angle of β1 = β2 = 0° or, if necessary, in all positions specified in Part 1 of Annex 4, paragraphs 1.1. and 1.2.
requirements.test_case: Measure the RI at 20' divergence and β1 = β2 = 0° after the oil test and compare it with the paragraph 5.1.4 limits.
requirements.why: This is the pass/fail criterion of the oil-resistance test for the moulded plastics Class IA retro-reflector P-05.
